title: ERP Integration Tools vs. Composable ERP: What Actually Fixes Reconciliation
summary: ERP integration tools move data between systems but don’t unify it. Composable ERP creates one source of truth across your stack in weeks.
body_text: Want to test drive the most customizable ERP platform in the market? If you’re evaluating tools like Celigo, Workato, or MuleSoft, it’s probably because reconciliation is eating away at your week. Numbers don’t match across systems, and someone is doing a lot of manual work to make everything line up. But ERP integration tools aren’t actually built to remove silos. They can move data faster and more reliably than a person using spreadsheets. At the end of the day, however, you’re still going to have separate systems that each have their own version of the truth. This piece walks through the basics of ERP integration tools, gives you a scorecard to help evaluate any option that’s on the table, and shows what composable ERP does differently — unifying those systems into a single source of truth rather than just connecting them faster. What You’ll Learn: The ERP integration tools landscape How to choose ERP integration tools Where ERP integration tools stop: Connecting systems vs. unifying them ERP integration tool vs. composable ERP The ERP Integration Tools Landscape An “ERP integration tool” is a type of software with five separate approaches (depending on how you draw the lines). If you’ve been looking for an integration tool, you’ve probably already come across two or three of these without realizing they’re structurally different. What’s important to know, however, is that the most important distinction between categories isn’t about which tool has the most connectors or the best UI. It’s about how each approach moves data between systems. Every approach listed here is essentially a connector. It’s built to move or expose data between systems that stay separate. But moving data around and having data you can trust are two different things. How to Choose ERP Integration Tools Before committing to a tool, it’s helpful to think about what problem you’re looking to solve: moving data between systems, or trusting the data you end up with. You can score any integration approach based on whether it centralizes truth; who’s responsible for fixing it when it breaks; and what happens as you scale up and add more tools. When you score the approaches from above on those three criteria, you’ll notice that each one of them fails on at least one axis as systems are added. No approach scores well across all three criteria. The ones that come the closest with data trust tend to be the ones that centralize something. Scalability is where things fall apart the most. What does it actually look like as connections stack up and this area becomes harder to manage? With every new system, you’re responsible for keeping more connections alive. More wiring doesn’t help with creating a single source of truth. It just increases the maintenance burden. Where ERP Integration Tools Stop: Connecting Systems vs. Unifying Them Even a perfectly-scored integration tool still runs into a wall. It wasn’t designed to create a system of record. It was designed to sync data between systems of record. For example, perhaps your inventory system says you have 40 units of a product, but your storefront says you have 42. Both are accurately reflecting the last sync that ran. They’re both “correct.” And yet, they disagree. Nobody messed up. The sync worked as it was designed. The issue is that “designed to sync eventually” and “true right now” are two different things. Adding more integrations doesn’t fix reconciliation. It just adds more gaps that need to be reconciled. To fix this — to get one record instead of moving data between two — you need an entirely different architecture. That architecture is a composable, headless ERP. A composable ERP lays a single backend under the tools you already use (like QuickBooks, Shopify, or ShipStation). Each tool continues doing its job, but it reads from and writes to the same underlying data layer in real time. There’s no longer a second copy of the data that needs to be synced. The number is the same everywhere. That should be the primary factor driving your ERP integration tool decision: whether you’re trying to move data faster between systems, or you’re trying to stop needing to move it at all. ERP Integration Tool vs. Composable ERP Integration tools connect what you have. Composable ERP unifies. The choice of which one is best for you depends on whether reconciliation is a symptom you’re managing, or a root cause you’re removing. Tailor is best-in-breed, not all-in-one. You’re not ripping out the tools your team is already familiar with. You’re replacing the duct tape underneath the tools. This quick guide can help you figure out whether an ERP integration tool or a composable ERP will best fit your current needs: If you’re connecting fewer than three systems, primarily for reporting/analytics, an integration tool is a reasonable fit. If you have a growing system count, reconciliation is a daily operational cost, and you need real-time accuracy, a composable ERP is the better choice. If an integration tool is sufficient for now, that answer is worth revisiting as your system count grows. If you landed on composable ERP, remember, you can reach unification without having to start from scratch. From ERP Integration Tools to One Source of Truth The reconciliation problem isn’t really about which ERP integration tool moves data the fastest or has the most connectors. It’s about whether you’re working from one number, or several numbers that are supposed to match. You don’t have to rip out your stack to get a single source of truth. Tailor unifies the tools you already run (QuickBooks, Shopify, ShipStation) into one backend, in weeks. See how Tailor can unify your existing tools into one source of truth.

title: Blood Pressure Medicine Recall: What Patients Need to Know About the Valsartan Warning

body_text: A blood pressure medicine has been recalled in the United States after a manufacturing issue raised concerns about whether the tablets dissolve properly. The recall affects a specific batch of valsartan, a commonly prescribed medicine used to control high blood pressure and treat certain heart conditions. The warning concerns Diovan, a brand of valsartan manufactured by Novartis. According to the information provided in the source article, the affected batch was recalled after failing dissolution specifications. This means the tablets may not break down and release the medicine into the body as expected, which could potentially reduce how effectively the treatment works. Which medicine has been recalled? The medicine involved is valsartan, an angiotensin II receptor blocker, often shortened to ARB. These medicines work by helping relax blood vessels, which can lower blood pressure and reduce the workload on the heart. Valsartan can be prescribed for hypertension and heart failure, and it may also be used for some patients following a heart attack. The source article explains that Diovan is one brand under which valsartan is sold. Importantly, the warning does not mean that every medicine containing valsartan has been recalled. Drug recalls generally apply to particular products, manufacturers, batches or lot numbers. The US Food and Drug Administration also advises patients to check the manufacturer, product details and lot number rather than assuming that every valsartan product is affected. Why has the batch been withdrawn? The reported reason for the recall is a failure to meet dissolution requirements. Dissolution testing is used to determine how a tablet breaks down and releases its active ingredient. If a tablet does not dissolve correctly, there is a possibility that the medicine may not be delivered into the body in the intended way. The article states that the affected valsartan product was recalled because of this issue and warns that the problem could affect its effectiveness. The affected batch is identified as AV5913C . The recalled packages contain 90 tablets of 160 mg each and have an expiration date of June 2027. According to the source, the tablets were manufactured by Pantheon Manufacturing Services in Greenville, North Carolina, and distributed by Novartis Pharmaceutical Corp. in Hanover, New Jersey. The recall was initially announced by Novartis on August 4, according to the report. What does a Class II recall mean? The report says the US Food and Drug Administration classified the notice as a Class II recall. A Class II classification generally indicates that exposure to the affected product could cause temporary or medically reversible health consequences. The source explains that the potential consequences are not expected to continue after the medicine is stopped, although they could still be harmful. This classification should not be interpreted as meaning that everyone who has taken the recalled medicine will experience a serious health problem. Recalls are issued as a safety measure when a product does not meet the required standards or presents a potential risk. The FDA describes drug recalls as an important way of protecting consumers when a medicine may be defective or potentially harmful. Should patients stop taking valsartan? Patients should not automatically stop taking a blood pressure medicine because they have seen a recall headline. Valsartan is used to manage important medical conditions, and suddenly stopping prescribed treatment without professional advice can create its own risks. The FDA advises patients taking recalled ARB medicines to continue their current medication until they receive advice and a replacement from a doctor or pharmacist. Anyone concerned about their medication should therefore check the packaging and speak with a pharmacist or doctor. A healthcare professional can determine whether the specific medicine and batch are included in the recall and, if necessary, arrange an alternative supply. This is particularly important because not every valsartan product is necessarily affected by a particular recall. Checking the exact product and batch information is more reliable than relying on the name of the medicine alone. How can patients check their medicine? The first step is to look at the prescription packaging or medicine label. Patients should check the name of the medicine, strength, manufacturer and lot or batch number. The FDA provides information about recalled ARB products and explains that these details can be used to identify whether a particular medicine is affected. If the information matches a recalled product, patients should contact their pharmacy or prescribing healthcare professional for guidance. Pharmacists may be able to provide an unaffected batch or discuss an appropriate alternative with the prescriber. Patients should also avoid making changes to their treatment without professional advice. Blood pressure medicines are normally taken regularly, and treatment decisions can depend on the patient's medical history and other medicines. Why medicine recalls matter Medicine recalls demonstrate why pharmaceutical manufacturers and regulators conduct detailed quality checks. A tablet must contain the correct active ingredient and meet standards for factors such as strength, purity and dissolution. Even when a problem affects only one batch, removing that batch from circulation can help reduce potential risks to patients. The FDA maintains information about recalled medicines and advises patients and healthcare professionals to check recall information when concerns arise. Its guidance also stresses that not every product containing an affected medicine is necessarily part of a recall. For people taking valsartan, the key message is therefore to avoid panic but take the warning seriously. Check the medicine packaging, identify the batch information and speak with a pharmacist or doctor if there is any possibility that the medication is affected. Sources US Food and Drug Administration, Recalls of Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers (ARBs) including Valsartan, Losartan and Irbesartan . US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Recalls . Express, reporting the August 13, 2026 valsartan recall and affected batch information. Disclaimer: This article is for general information only and is not medical advice. Recall information can change, and patients should check official regulatory information and speak with a pharmacist, doctor or other qualified healthcare professional about their individual medication. Do not stop or change prescribed treatment without professional guidance.

title: CSX Customer Advisory: Severe Weather Impacts Chicago and Northwest Indiana Operations
summary: CSX is a leading supplier of rail-based freight transportation in North America. But there's more to CSX than you might expect. Learn all about CSX and discover what we're doing for our customers, environment and communities. Visit http://www.csx.com/.
body_text: CSX Customer Advisory: Severe Weather Impacts Chicago and Northwest Indiana Operations August 11, 2026 CSX is responding to operational impacts from a destructive line of severe storms and tornadoes that moved through the Chicago metropolitan area and Northwest Indiana today, causing widespread damage and power outages across the region. The severe weather is affecting CSX operations on the Monon and Garrett subdivisions. In advance of the storms, trains in affected areas were held in accordance with wind-related safety protocols. As the storm system continues moving east, our Engineering teams are actively assessing track and infrastructure conditions and working to clear storm-related obstructions. Severe thunderstorm and flood watches remain in effect, and additional weather-related impacts are possible. Customers with shipments moving through the affected region should expect delays while recovery efforts continue. We will restore normal train operations as conditions permit and once routes are confirmed safe for movement. We will continue to provide updates as needed. For the latest network information, please refer to CSX Customer Advisories and Intermodal Real-Time Service Advisories. If your facility experiences a closure or changes in local service needs because of the severe weather, please notify your CSX representative as soon as possible so we can coordinate support and adjust service plans accordingly. For assistance with shipment inquiries, contact the CSX Customer Solutions team at 1-877-ShipCSX (1-877-744-7279). For Carload assistance: Select option 2, then 1, then 5. For Intermodal assistance: Select option 2, then 2, then 2. You may also submit a Shipment Problem Resolution request via our website: www.shipcsx.com . Thank you for your patience and partnership as we work to safely restore normal operations.

title: What Buy with AWS Does to Your Website Funnel
summary: Buy with AWS turns your website into a purchase surface. What changes in the funnel, what the buyer needs, and what breaks if the page is not ready.
body_text: Buy with AWS lets a visitor start and finish an AWS Marketplace purchase from your own website. It does not add a step to your funnel — it removes the step where your team qualified the buyer, which means the page has to do that job instead. The pitch is easy to like. A prospect reads your product page, clicks a button, and buys through AWS Marketplace without ever asking you for a quote. Procurement is already solved, billing is consolidated, and nobody had to schedule a call. The part worth thinking about before you add the button is what disappears. In the funnel you have today, someone talks to that prospect before money changes hands — and in that conversation they establish which AWS account is involved, whether the buyer can actually purchase, and whether the deal should have been a private offer instead. Buy with AWS removes the conversation. It does not remove the questions. What is Buy with AWS? Buy with AWS is a set of calls-to-action a seller places on their own website that let a visitor transact in AWS Marketplace without leaving that site. AWS describes it as “a streamlined way to find, try, and buy products from Partner sites.” The buyer flow is four steps: Find a product marked Available in AWS Marketplace on the partner’s site Select Buy with AWS Sign in with an AWS account Complete the transaction on a co-branded procurement page The charge then behaves like any other marketplace purchase — it “becomes part of your AWS bill,” and AWS pays the seller. What actually changes in the funnel The buttons do not sit at the bottom of the funnel. They sit wherever you put them, which is usually much higher than the point where your sales process currently starts. The page becomes the qualification step. Previously a form captured a lead and a human decided whether this was a marketplace deal, a direct deal, or nothing. Now the visitor decides, using only what is on the page. If the page does not say what the product costs, what the commitment is, or what happens after purchase, the visitor either buys the wrong thing or does not buy. Self-serve and negotiated paths now share a surface. A visitor who should have been a private offer will happily buy at list price — which is a smaller deal than the one you would have written — while an enterprise buyer who needs custom terms will click the button, find no route to them, and leave. Both are failures of the same page. Support arrives before onboarding does. A purchase you did not know was happening produces an entitlement you were not expecting. Everything downstream of that — provisioning, welcome email, account mapping — has to work without a human trigger. When a buyer pays and provisioning never happens is the failure mode this makes more likely, not less. What the buyer needs, and what it screens out AWS is specific: the buyer needs “an AWS account with a valid payment method and the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) credentials required to make a purchase through AWS Marketplace.” Three separate things, and a visitor can fail any of them: Requirement Who fails it An AWS account Prospects evaluating on behalf of a company that uses another cloud A valid payment method Accounts that transact only under an enterprise agreement IAM permission to subscribe Almost every engineer, in almost every large company The third is the interesting one, because it is invisible until the click. The person most likely to be reading your product page — an engineer evaluating the tool — is the person least likely to hold marketplace purchasing rights. AWS also notes that “your existing governance and controls will apply to Buy with AWS purchases.” A buyer whose organisation restricts which products may be subscribed to will be blocked by their own policy on your page. Nothing about your site caused it, and nothing about your site can fix it. This is not an argument against the button. It is an argument for what sits next to it. What to put beside the button A second path. Every Buy with AWS call-to-action should have a visible alternative for the buyer who cannot use it — “request a private offer,” pointing somewhere a human answers. Without it, the highest-value visitors have nowhere to go. Enough price to decide. A purchase button on a page with no pricing asks the visitor to start a transaction to find out what it costs. Most will not. A statement of what happens next. Say what arrives after purchase and how quickly. This is the copy that converts a hesitant self-serve buyer, and it is the copy most product pages lack. Consistency with the listing. The product page and the AWS Marketplace listing are now two views of one purchase. Dimensions, plan names and units that disagree between them produce a buyer who thinks they bought something else. The listing readiness checklist covers what the listing side has to get right. Measuring it honestly The temptation is to read every Buy with AWS purchase as incremental revenue. Some of it is displacement: deals that would have closed anyway, now closing at list price instead of at a negotiated one, and without the multi-year term a private offer would have carried. That is not automatically bad — faster and smaller can beat slower and larger — but it is a different result from “we added a channel.” Compare the deals that came through the button against the ones your team wrote by hand: size, term length, and whether they renew. Four metrics to watch after you add Buy with AWS covers what AWS reports on the traffic side; the comparison against your own pipeline is the one only you can run. Frequently asked questions What is Buy with AWS? A set of calls-to-action a seller places on their own website that let a visitor discover and purchase the seller’s AWS Marketplace product without leaving that site, completing on a co-branded AWS procurement page. Does the buyer need an AWS account? Yes. AWS requires an AWS account with a valid payment method and the IAM credentials needed to make an AWS Marketplace purchase. Can a private offer be sent through Buy with AWS? The button transacts a purchase; negotiated terms are still a private offer. Pair the button with a visible route to request one, or enterprise buyers have no path. Will a buyer’s own controls block the purchase? They can. AWS states that a buyer’s existing governance and controls apply to Buy with AWS purchases, so an organisation that restricts subscribable products will block it regardless of your setup. Does Buy with AWS replace the AWS Marketplace listing? No. It is an additional entry point to the same listing, so the two must agree on pricing, plans and dimensions. What breaks first after adding it? Provisioning. Purchases now arrive without a human trigger, so any onboarding step that assumed a warm handoff has to work automatically. Takeaways Buy with AWS moves qualification onto your product page. The page has to answer what a salesperson used to. The buyer needs an AWS account, a payment method, and IAM purchasing rights — and the reader most likely to be on your page usually lacks the third. The buyer’s own governance applies, so some visitors are blocked by policies you cannot see or change. Always pair the button with a visible route to a private offer, or the largest deals have nowhere to go. Purchases now arrive with no human trigger, so provisioning has to be fully automatic before the button goes on the page. Measure against your own pipeline, not just AWS’s dashboard, to see how much is new revenue and how much is displaced. Adding a purchase button is the easy half. See how Suger’s AWS Marketplace seller solution keeps the listing, the offers and the entitlements behind it consistent, so a purchase from your own site provisions exactly like one from the marketplace catalogue.

title: James Hardie to Expand Regional Distribution Partnerships
summary: Builds on longstanding regional partnerships to broaden access to James Hardie’s complete portfolio of exterior building products, adding Hardie® siding and trim to existing product offerings
body_text: CHICAGO – August 3, 2026 – James Hardie Building Products Inc. (“James Hardie”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of James Hardie Industries plc (“JHI”) (NYSE / ASX: JHX), today announced expanded portfolio arrangements with several of its existing regional distributors to include James Hardie’s complete portfolio of exterior building products, alongside that of its North American affiliates’, in select locations: Capital Lumber Company (“Capital Lumber”), Dixie Plywood and Lumber Company (“DIXIEPLY"), Lumbermen’s Inc. (“Lumbermen’s”), Parksite, Woodgrain, and Woolf Distributing. The participating distributors will carry the company’s complete portfolio for the first time, adding Hardie® siding and trim to their product lines alongside existing AZEK® and TimberTech® product offerings, across designated markets. “We are pleased to build upon our longstanding regional relationships with Capital Lumber, DIXIEPLY, Lumbermen’s, Parksite, Woodgrain, and Woolf Distributing,” said Aaron Erter, CEO of JHI. “These expanded relationships are an important step in bringing the full strength of our unified portfolio to market. By creating a more connected distribution network, we will make it even easier for customers to access our trusted products and excellent service, driving long-term value creation.” The arrangements are part of James Hardie’s broader effort to strengthen how its portfolio is brought to market across the United States. As noted in a separate press release issued here today, James Hardie also announced that Boise Cascade Company (“Boise Cascade”) will become the sole U.S. nationwide distributor of James Hardie’s and its North American affiliates’ complete portfolio of exterior building products through its extensive network of strategically located distribution facilities across the United States, effective July 31, 2026. About James Hardie Building Products Inc. James Hardie Building Products Inc. is the North American leader in fiber cement siding and exterior design solutions and part of the larger James Hardie group of companies that offer a portfolio of leading exterior and outdoor living brands including Hardie®, TimberTech®, AZEK®, Versatex®, and StruXure®. As The Home of Resilient Beauty™, its products are trusted by architects, builders, contractors, and homeowners throughout North America. title: The QR Codes You Can't Scan
summary: Pay local merchants by QR code across Asia and Latin America. Connect your bank or card, skip ATM fees, and pay like a local in your own currency with Moreta.
body_text: The QR Codes You Can't Scan The mango sticky rice lady on Sukhumvit Soi 38 has a QR code taped to her cart, and it is not for you. It's for the office workers ahead of you in line, who scan it with their Thai banking apps and drift off without breaking conversation. You, meanwhile, are holding a phone with three banking apps, two travel cards, and Apple Pay — a small fortune in fintech — and none of it can read that little black-and-white square. She takes your crumpled banknote with the practiced patience of someone who deals with tourists all day. Here's the uncomfortable truth about Asia's cashless revolution: it wasn't built for visitors. We've written about how QR payments swallowed Cambodia , China , and Argentina — but every one of those stories has a footnote that matters enormously if you're the one traveling: these systems run on local bank accounts , and you don't have one. The Membership Problem Take Thailand, where the national PromptPay system handles the daily payments of an entire country. The catch for a visitor is that PromptPay is tied to a Thai bank account or Thai phone number — neither of which tourists can realistically get. Your Revolut card, your Wise account, your home banking app: to the noodle stall's QR code, they simply don't exist. Thaiger It gets more specific than that. Thai vendors use two kinds of codes — merchant QRs issued through banks and payment processors, and personal QRs tied to an individual's phone number or ID. Street food stalls, market vendors, and taxis overwhelmingly use the personal kind, which doesn't accept foreign payment apps or cards at all. So the fancier the restaurant, the more likely your card works — and the better the food, the more likely it doesn't. There's probably a law of travel in there somewhere. Blogarama "Just Use Your Card" Doesn't Survive Contact With a Night Market The standard advice — bring a Visa, you'll be fine — holds up right until you leave the mall. Foreign cards work at hotels, chain restaurants, and shopping centres; street vendors and small shops remain cash-only from a card's point of view. Even the tap-to-pay ecosystem has a velvet rope: Apple Pay and Google Pay work at 7-Eleven and the big chains, but not at independent shops. New Asia LivingNew Asia Living And this isn't a Thailand quirk. The same pattern repeats in Vietnam with VietQR, in Indonesia with QRIS, in Malaysia with DuitNow. The systems are brilliant — genuinely some of the best payment infrastructure on earth — but they're brilliant for locals . The tourist experience is standing in a country that has largely stopped using cash, holding nothing but cash. The Club Within the Club Here's the twist that makes it sting a little more. If you're traveling within Asia, the walls are already coming down. Visitors from China, Malaysia, Singapore, Vietnam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Hong Kong, Korea, and Japan can scan Thai QR codes directly from their own home banking apps — an arrangement confirmed by the Bank of Thailand. The ASEAN payment connectivity initiative has stitched national QR systems together so that a traveler's home bank or e-wallet works across borders. wise A Malaysian in Bangkok scans and pays like she's at home. A Singaporean in Phnom Penh, same thing. The region has quietly built a scannable club — and if your bank is in London, Sydney, or Chicago, you're not in it. The Workaround Industry Where there's friction, there's a cottage industry. Thailand alone has spawned a whole genre of tourist-wallet workarounds: apps like TAGTHAi that you top up at bank exchange booths in airports and department stores before you can scan anything, and local wallets whose signup process has become travel-blog folklore. One popular method involves withdrawing baht from an ATM with a foreign card, then walking into a 7-Eleven to deposit that cash over the counter into a local wallet — which is a lot of steps to avoid carrying the cash you just withdrew. Even then, foreigner accounts are often restricted to store payments and blocked from scanning the personal QR codes that street vendors actually use. wise + 2 Every one of these hacks works, sort of, in one country, with effort. Cross a border and you start over: new wallet, new verification, new exchange booth, new folklore. What to Actually Do The honest playbook for Southeast Asia right now looks like this. Keep a foreign card for hotels, malls, and anywhere with air conditioning and a printed receipt. Carry a modest amount of local cash, because a few holdouts will always want it. And for everything in between — the night markets, the tuk-tuks, the noodle carts, which is to say the entire reason you came — you need something that speaks the local QR language without demanding a local bank account. That last piece is exactly what Moreta is: one wallet, topped up once, that scans local payment codes across Southeast Asia — so the mango sticky rice lady's QR code is finally for you too. Download the app before you fly, and skip the 7-Eleven cash-deposit pilgrimage entirely.

title: Publix Expands Frozen Berry Recall After E. Coli Outbreak Sickens 12
summary: Food safety remains a top priority for consumers, and the latest recall involving Publix GreenWise frozen berries has raised fresh concerns across several U.S. states. body_text: Food safety remains a top priority for consumers, and the latest recall involving Publix GreenWise frozen berries has raised fresh concerns across several U.S. states. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has expanded a previous recall to include all GreenWise Organic Whole Blueberries and Whole Mixed Berries after an investigation linked the products to an E. coli outbreak that has sickened 12 people. The recall affects multiple package sizes and products distributed across eight states. Health officials are urging customers to immediately check their freezers, discard any affected products, or return them to the store for a refund. In this article, we explain why the recall was expanded, which products are affected, the health risks associated with E. coli infection, and what consumers should do if they have purchased these frozen berries. FDA Expands Publix Frozen Berry Recall The FDA announced that Publix has voluntarily expanded its frozen berry recall after investigators identified additional concerns during an ongoing food safety investigation. Initially, the recall involved only one lot of GreenWise Organic IQF Blueberries. However, new findings prompted officials to broaden the recall to include every GreenWise Organic Whole Blueberries and Whole Mixed Berries product in both 10-ounce and 48-ounce packaging. The agency believes the expanded recall is necessary to protect consumers while investigators continue determining the exact source of contamination. Health officials recommend that anyone who purchased these products should not consume them under any circumstances. Recalled GreenWise Frozen Berry Products The expanded recall includes the following GreenWise frozen berry products: GreenWise Organic Whole Blueberries, 10-ounce package, UPC 41415-06453 GreenWise Organic Whole Blueberries, 48-ounce package, UPC 41415-12053 GreenWise Organic Whole Mixed Berries, 10-ounce package, UPC 41415-06753 GreenWise Organic Whole Mixed Berries, 48-ounce package, UPC 41415-12153 These products were sold at Publix stores in: Alabama Florida Georgia Kentucky North Carolina South Carolina Tennessee Virginia Consumers are encouraged to inspect their freezers carefully. If the original packaging has been removed and there is no way to identify the berries, the FDA advises throwing them away as a precaution. E. Coli Outbreak Sickens 12 People According to federal health officials, 12 confirmed illnesses have been linked to the outbreak. Reported cases occurred in Florida and Georgia, with illness onset dates ranging from May 11 through June 5. Four people required hospitalization due to the severity of their infections. Fortunately, no deaths have been reported at the time of writing. The FDA stated that interviews with affected individuals consistently pointed toward GreenWise organic frozen blueberries sold at Publix as the primary food consumed before illness. The investigation remains active, and additional cases could still be identified. Source of the Contamination Investigators traced the frozen blueberries to Frutas y Hortalizas del Sur S.A., a supplier located in San Carlos, Chile. Following a review of company records and food safety procedures, the FDA identified concerns involving more than one shipment of blueberries supplied to Publix. Because of these findings, the agency expanded the recall beyond the original lot and warned that additional products connected to the supplier could be added if new evidence emerges. The FDA also noted concerns regarding other products from the same supplier that have not entered the U.S. market. FDA Places Supplier Under Import Alert As part of its response, the FDA placed frozen blueberries and blueberry-containing berry mixes from Frutas y Hortalizas del Sur S.A. on Import Alert 99-35. This action allows federal inspectors to detain covered shipments entering the United States without conducting routine physical inspections. Import alerts are used when regulators believe imported food products may violate U.S. safety standards, helping prevent potentially contaminated products from reaching consumers. Understanding E. Coli O145:H28 The outbreak involves a dangerous strain known as E. coli O145:H28 . Although many strains of E. coli are harmless, this particular type can cause serious foodborne illness. Common symptoms include: Severe stomach cramps Diarrhea Bloody diarrhea in some cases Nausea Vomiting Fever Symptoms generally appear several days after consuming contaminated food. While many healthy adults recover within about a week, certain individuals face a higher risk of serious complications. Serious Health Risks One of the most severe complications associated with E. coli infection is hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) , a condition that can cause kidney failure. Those at greatest risk include: Young children Older adults Individuals with weakened immune systems Anyone experiencing severe symptoms after eating recalled frozen berries should seek medical attention immediately. Prompt medical evaluation is especially important if bloody diarrhea, dehydration, or reduced urination develops. What Consumers Should Do The FDA recommends taking the following steps if you have purchased GreenWise frozen berries: Stop eating the recalled products immediately. Throw the berries away or return them to the store for a refund. Clean and sanitize any containers, utensils, or surfaces that came into contact with the berries. Monitor for symptoms of E. coli infection. Contact a healthcare provider if symptoms develop after consuming the recalled products. Even if the berries appear normal, freezing does not eliminate harmful bacteria, making disposal the safest option. Earlier Recall Expanded Publix originally recalled only one lot of GreenWise Organic IQF Blueberries on July 3. That initial recall covered: Lot code: 60401 Printed as: 6 040 01 Best-by date: February 9, 2028 Following additional investigation, regulators determined that contamination concerns could extend beyond that single lot, leading to the broader recall announced on July 29 and supported by the FDA on July 30. Ongoing Investigation Federal, state, and local health agencies continue working together to determine how contamination occurred. Investigators are reviewing production records, supply chain information, and testing data to identify the precise source of the outbreak. The FDA has indicated that more products could be added to the recall if additional evidence links them to the contamination. Consumers should continue checking FDA recall updates and Publix announcements for the latest information. Final Thoughts The expanded Publix frozen berry recall highlights the importance of food safety monitoring and rapid public health responses. While only 12 illnesses have been confirmed so far, the FDA is taking precautionary measures by recalling all affected GreenWise frozen berry products and restricting future imports from the identified supplier. If you purchased GreenWise Organic Whole Blueberries or Whole Mixed Berries from Publix, check your freezer immediately. Do not consume any recalled products, even if they look or smell normal. Following FDA guidance can help reduce the risk of serious illness and protect your household from foodborne infection. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) food safety guidance. Information provided in the source article by Kelly McBride Ni, published by NTD Television on July 31, 2026. If you believe you have become ill after consuming a recalled product, consult a qualified healthcare professional immediately.

title: Intapp Compliance with Celeste: Accept more business, faster — without increasing risk
summary: Intapp Celeste is now embedded directly inside Intapp Intake, Conflicts, and Terms, so your firm can confidently take on more business faster.
body_text: As firms grow through lateral hiring, private capital investment, and M&A and geographic expansion, the volume of new business rises — and so does the compliance work required to accept it. Every new engagement requires teams to clear intake, conflicts, and client obligations before it can be billed. The repetitive steps that stand between experts and their judgment limit how much a firm can accept. In July, we announced the general availability of Intapp Celeste , our agentic AI platform for professional firms that’s grounded in your firm’s knowledge and policies. Now, Celeste is embedded directly inside Intapp Intake , Conflicts , and Terms . Your professionals can work with Celeste in the products they use every day, handing routine setup work to agentic playbooks and asking questions about their compliance data in plain language. Preparation, not decision-making, is the real bottleneck Compliance work depends on expert judgment. But before an analyst can weigh a conflict or clear a request, the search must be built, the details gathered and validated, the corporate structures mapped, and the context assembled. Most of that preparation is repetitive, high-volume work that consumes hours and rarely calls for the analyst’s expertise. The burden doesn’t fall on compliance teams alone. The professionals who win the work must also conduct the same preparation work — completing intake forms manually, responding to follow-up questions, and waiting for clearance — before they can begin billing. The effect compounds across the firm: Time-to-bill slows, new business stalls, and skilled professionals are pulled away from the higher-risk questions that need their attention. Traditionally, firms have met growing compliance demands by adding headcount. But today’s growth is outpacing that model. Every lateral team, acquisition, and new office adds volume faster than a firm can recruit and train analysts to clear it. Celeste offers a different approach by handling the preparatory tasks, allowing experts to remain in control of and provide judgment on every decision. Celeste lifts the ceiling for compliance Business acceptance workflows represent some of a firm’s most repetitive, high-volume compliance work. Celeste follows the same workflows your teams do, supporting every stage of the client lifecycle — from intake and conflicts clearance to ongoing client obligations. Business intake: The moment an email arrives, professionals can ask Intapp Celeste to open a new intake request — without leaving Outlook. Celeste extracts details from the email to auto-populate the form, then validates each answer in real time as the requestor reviews, edits, and completes the request. It also offers recommended enhancements before submission, so compliance teams can begin their assessment with complete, accurate requests — accelerating time-to-bill. Conflicts clearance: The moment a request arrives, Celeste builds the search strategy, matches corporate trees for each party, and runs the search automatically. It then triages the results for expert review, surfacing likely conflicts and helping to clear low-risk items faster. Celeste can also automatically draft the clearance summary, pulling together resolved hits and the details that matter, with a clear record of how each was resolved. Terms and client obligations management: When outside counsel guidelines arrive — through Outlook or the Intapp Celeste panel — Celeste reads them, matches them to the right client records, populates the key attributes, and categorizes the terms. It automatically ingests new guidelines from a shared inbox and categorizes them in Terms within seconds, eliminating manual cataloging. Firms can also enforce configured terms — like block billing or restricted words — to auto-accept during AI categorization. The terms will flow straight into downstream applications like Time the moment Celeste ingests the new guidelines document — no handoff required. Compliance intelligence: An embedded Celeste panel sits directly in Intapp Intake, Conflicts, and Terms — giving professionals one place to ask questions about their compliance data in plain language and run routine playbooks. Answers are drawn from the firm’s own records, link back to the source for verification, and are grounded in the firm’s access policies. Risk and firm leaders get immediate answers during compliance procedures, strategic planning, and regulatory responses. Celeste reflects how professional firms actually work Unlike generic AI tools and point solutions — which require firms to adjust their workflows — Celeste is built for the professional services workflows your teams rely on today. It handles the repetitive tasks that precede every decision while allowing the expert to remain in control of the decision itself. That balance is what governed AI looks like in a regulated firm. Celeste handles the preparatory work. Experts remain in control of every decision. And every step — the analysis and rationale behind each request, workflow, and decision — is documented. Firms accept more business faster, and every decision carries a clear account of how it was reached. What’s next? This is just the beginning. We’ll continue to introduce new ways for Celeste to support your teams and to put your compliance data to work across every workflow. The future is continuous compliance, where risks are identified, surfaced, and addressed before they become problems. Learn more about how Intapp Compliance with Celeste works across the client lifecycle, or talk with your Intapp account team.

title: Nutanix and ChronoScale Announce Strategic Partnership to Accelerate Enterprise AI Adoption
summary: Nutanix and ChronoScale plan to integrate their platforms so enterprises can extend into ChronoScale GPU-as-a-Service, pre-paid inference tokens through ChronoScale Token Factory, and a locally-deployed ChronoScale Foundry for enterprise agentic AI...
body_text: Nutanix and ChronoScale plan to integrate their platforms so enterprises can extend into ChronoScale GPU-as-a-Service, pre-paid inference tokens through ChronoScale Token Factory, and a locally-deployed ChronoScale Foundry for enterprise agentic AI workflows ChronoScale to leverage Nutanix Agentic AI software solution for neoclouds to deliver broad portfolio of accelerated compute and AI services Collaboration extends to go-to-market, joint solution development, technical integration, and customer engagement programs San Jose, Calif. and Menlo Park, Calif. – Aug. 18, 2026 – Nutanix (NASDAQ: NTNX ), a hybrid cloud leader and AI innovator, and ChronoScale Holdings Corporation (NASDAQ: CHRN), an accelerated compute platform purpose-built to support demanding artificial intelligence workloads, today announced a strategic partnership to jointly deliver enterprise-ready AI infrastructure and help accelerate adoption of AI services across global markets. The partnership brings together complementary capabilities enterprise customers have historically had to assemble themselves — combining Nutanix's full portfolio of agentic AI solutions with ChronoScale's accelerated compute, enterprise AI foundry, and outcome-driven delivery model. ChronoScale and Nutanix Platform Integration ChronoScale plans to leverage Nutanix software within its AI infrastructure platform to help deliver a broad portfolio of accelerated compute and AI services. The parties expect Nutanix software to help support customer onboarding, tenant management, service automation, virtualized infrastructure, managed Kubernetes environments, and advanced AI service offerings. ChronoScale's platform is designed to support a broad ecosystem of technology partners. The companies also intend to jointly maintain demonstration and proof-of-concept environments to support customer evaluations and accelerate adoption of agentic AI solutions in the enterprise. Extended GPU capacity, on-premises and beyond ChronoScale plans to extend the Nutanix on-premises cloud footprint with elastic access to modern GPU capacity. Customers are expected to be able to procure reserved capacity through ChronoScale GPU-as-a-Service (GPUaaS) for predictable workloads, or draw on ChronoScale Token Factory — pre-paid inference tokens backed by leading open-source models — for burst and experimental workloads. The parties intend to integrate both offerings with the Nutanix enterprise AI offerings, including Agent Gateway and Private Inferencing, with the goal of providing customers a single control plane across their on-premises environment and ChronoScale capacity. ChronoScale Foundry, delivered through Nutanix Nutanix will enable the deployment of ChronoScale Foundry, an enterprise AI foundry, inside the customer's own environment, giving enterprises a managed platform to build, run, and govern agentic workflows locally. Agents, enterprise data, and workflow state remain within the customer's boundary. Enterprise customers are expected to be able to deploy Foundry directly through the Nutanix Kubernetes Platform Catalog, extending Nutanix's AI portfolio into managed agentic workloads. The partnership is designed to help enterprises globally deploy production-scale AI environments faster, with greater operational simplicity, sovereignty, security, and scalability. The partnership being announced today is underpinned by the strategic relationship and technology partnership that both ChronoScale and Nutanix have with NVIDIA. Chronoscale is an NVIDIA Cloud Partner (NCP), delivering an accelerated computing platform, built and optimized using NVIDIA-validated reference designs to deliver consistent performance at scale. Nutanix is an NVIDIA technology partner and ISV that has a suite of NVIDIA validated software to operate enterprise AI factories. Together, ChronoScale and Nutanix intend to deliver an integrated platform built on NVIDIA AI economics that is designed to reduce operational complexity and accelerate time-to-value for enterprises adopting AI at scale. ChronoScale plans to deploy NVIDIA HGX B300 systems interconnected via NVIDIA Spectrum-X networking and NVIDIA AI Enterprise software, including NVIDIA NIM microservices and NVIDIA NeMo to deliver a production-ready stack. title: Verto Taps Flagright for Cross-Border Payment Monitoring
summary: Verto selects Flagright for real-time transaction monitoring across its cross-border payments and FX infrastructure, with auditable, risk-based workflows.
body_text: Flagright, the AI native, no code platform for transaction monitoring and AML compliance, today announced that Verto has selected Flagright to strengthen financial crime controls across its cross-border payments and FX infrastructure. Verto will use Flagright to monitor transaction risk in real time and run investigations with auditable, risk-based workflows built for scale. Verto is building cross-border payments infrastructure that helps businesses operate globally with local capabilities. Through its platform, customers can open multi-currency accounts, accept native currency payments, convert at competitive rates, and execute high-speed global transfers. Verto supports payment acceptance from 190+ countries, local account opening in 50 countries, and processes 25B+ global payments annually. “As we scale global payments, controls have to scale with the same speed and consistency as the product,” said Ola Oyetayo, Co founder and CEO at Verto. “We need real-time visibility across complex flows and corridors, with monitoring that supports fast decision-making and clear documentation. Flagright gives us a risk-based monitoring layer that helps protect customers while keeping operations efficient.” “From a compliance operations perspective, consistency and evidence matter,” said Conor O'Kane, Compliance Operations Manager at Verto. “Flagright gives our team structured workflows to triage and investigate effectively, with clear audit trails that support strong governance across markets and payment types.” With Flagright, Verto will be able to: Monitor transactions in real time with configurable, risk-based controls across key payment and account flows Triage alerts efficiently and investigate activity with consistent workflows and clear decision trails Improve operational oversight with analytics and reporting that support evidence based decisions “Verto is building global payments and FX infrastructure at meaningful scale, across many markets and currencies,” said Baran Özkan, Co founder and CEO at Flagright. “We are excited to support their team with real-time transaction monitoring and auditable workflows that help them scale with confidence while keeping trust and compliance at the center of every flow.” About Verto Verto is a cross-border payment company that provides tools for collections, payouts and foreign exchange to startups, scaleups and enterprise companies. With the unique ability to support cross-border payments in emerging markets in Africa, Verto can help you do business with the world. About Flagright Flagright is a global leader in AI native transaction monitoring and AML compliance solutions, featuring a highly customizable, risk based platform with the industry’s fastest two week integration, enabling financial institutions to centralize detection, investigate and report suspicious activity, streamline regulatory workflows, and strengthen financial crime controls. Flagright has also been recognized as the fastest growing AML compliance platform in Europe on Sifted’s Europe 250 in 2025, also globally recognized by Chartis as a leader in AI for fincrime compliance in Chartis’s Financial Crime and Compliance50 2025, amongst several other global recognitions. Trusted by fintechs and banks in 30+ countries, Flagright helps reduce false positives by 93% and lower compliance costs by 80%, thereby setting the modern standard for financial crime compliance.

title: The Best Family Cars for Road Trips in 2026
summary: Planning a family road trip involves a lot of moving parts, but choosing the right vehicle can make the difference between a stressful slog and a memorable adventure.
body_text: Planning a family road trip involves a lot of moving parts, but choosing the right vehicle can make the difference between a stressful slog and a memorable adventure. The best family cars for road trips are designed to prioritize passenger comfort, ample cargo space, and everyday usability over long distances. Whether you are navigating interstate highways or winding scenic routes, having a cabin that keeps everyone relaxed, entertained, and comfortable is essential for a successful journey. Today’s market offers a variety of compelling options tailored to different travel needs, from traditional minivans with unbeatable interior flexibility to high-tech electric vehicles that make charging stops predictable and convenient. In this guide, we highlight standout models that excel at eating up the miles, including spacious haulers like the Chrysler Pacifica and Cadillac Escalade ESV, as well as highly efficient alternatives like the Toyota Sienna and Hyundai Ioniq 5. By focusing on the features that matter most—like quiet rides, intuitive technology, and generous legroom—you can find a vehicle that perfectly suits your family's next getaway. The standard 3.6-liter V6 makes 287 hp and 262 lb-ft of torque, paired with a nine-speed automatic, and it’s tuned more for smooth, stable cruising than sporty responses—an approach that helps keep passengers comfortable over long distances. If your trips include a camper or small trailer, the Pacifica’s available 3,600-pound towing capacity adds flexibility, while AWD availability on most trims can be a plus for year-round travel in wet or snowy regions. Inside, Chrysler’s minivan know-how shows up in family-friendly packaging and everyday convenience. Available Stow ‘n Go seating lets the second-row seats fold into the floor (and doubles as in-floor storage when the seats are up), and non-hybrid models provide 32.3 cubic feet of cargo space behind the third row, 87.5 behind the second row, and 140.5 with the second and third rows folded—useful numbers when you’re hauling suitcases, a cooler, and road-trip gear. Up front, a standard 10.1-inch Uconnect 5 touchscreen brings wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and features like available rear-seat entertainment and an interior FamCam help keep kids occupied and visible on the move. Safety tech such as automatic emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, and adaptive cruise control comes standard, and EPA ratings of up to 22 mpg combined (FWD) keep fuel stops reasonable for a V6 minivan. The Escalade ESV is also a tech-forward road-trip machine, thanks to its dramatic curved 38-inch OLED display (three screens under one sweeping panel), lots of connectivity (wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, wireless charging, and seven USB ports), and a standard 19-speaker AKG audio system with an available 36-speaker upgrade. On the highway, the Odyssey’s 3.5-liter V6 (280 hp, 262 lb-ft of torque) and 10-speed automatic make merging and passing feel effortless, and its ride/handling balance is unusually natural for a family hauler. With its 800-volt architecture, the Ioniq 5 can charge from 10% to 80% in about 20 minutes on a fast charger (up to 250 kW) with a CCS adapter, and it includes a NACS adapter for Tesla Superchargers, though those typically top out at 150 kW (about 30 minutes for the same 10%–80% window on the larger battery). A great road-trip car prioritizes passenger comfort, ample cargo space, and a smooth ride. Features like multi-zone climate control, abundant USB charging ports, supportive seating, and advanced driver-assistance systems (like adaptive cruise control) help reduce fatigue for both the driver and passengers over long distances. Are minivans still the best option for road trips? For many families, yes. Minivans like the Chrysler Pacifica, Honda Odyssey, and Toyota Sienna offer unmatched interior space, easy access via sliding doors, and flexible seating configurations. They typically provide more cargo room behind the third row than comparable three-row SUVs, making them incredibly practical for hauling luggage and gear. Can I take a family road trip in an electric vehicle (EV)? Absolutely. Modern EVs like the Hyundai Ioniq 5 and Lucid Gravity are excellent for road trips thanks to their quiet cabins, long driving ranges, and fast-charging capabilities. With a bit of route planning to utilize DC fast chargers, you can easily incorporate charging stops into your natural rest and meal breaks. Is a hybrid vehicle worth it for long drives? Hybrids are highly beneficial for road trips because they significantly reduce fuel costs and the frequency of gas station stops. Vehicles like the Toyota Sienna (which is hybrid-only) and the Hyundai Palisade Hybrid offer excellent fuel economy without sacrificing the space and power needed for highway cruising. How important is cargo space when choosing a road-trip car? It is crucial. You need enough room not just for suitcases, but for coolers, strollers, and other travel gear without encroaching on passenger legroom. When evaluating cargo space, look at the cubic feet available behind the rearmost seats you plan to use, as this represents your actual usable luggage capacity during the trip. title: Genetic Testing Pricing Transparency
summary: Probably Genetic offers truly no-cost genetic testing for eligible patients with rare diseases. Backed by research partnerships, the program eliminates surprise medical bills and insurance hassles. This guide explains how the free testing works, what data is collected (and what isn't), and how patients can apply in five simple steps—all with full price transparency and a mission to end the diagnostic odyssey.
body_text: Free genetic testing for rare diseases: complete price transparency guide Getting a genetic test shouldn't mean choosing between answers and financial hardship. Unlike other genetic testing companies that can surprise families with bills of thousands of dollars, our free testing programs ensure eligible patients receive comprehensive testing at absolutely no cost. Yes, it's truly no-cost if you're approved for one of our free testing programs. ‍ No-cost rare disease testing It's no surprise that our healthcare system continues to face systemic problems with billing practices and communication. It is a surprise, however, to our patients and families, that our no-cost testing programs are truly just that; free genetic testing for patients approved for one of our programs. In this article, we will outline how we can offer free testing and provide clarity on what we collect and do not collect as a company, in the interest of full transparency regarding our billing practices. ‍ How free genetic testing works for rare disease patients We partner with drug researchers, developers, and patient advocacy organizations to study and understand patient populations with specific genetic variants (or mutations). We achieve this by creating programs within specific disease areas, with the goal of helping to diagnose patients with specific genetic conditions where there is research being done to improve treatment options As an example, we have a program for WHIM syndrome (warts, hypogammaglobulinemia, frequent infections, and myelokathexis), which is driven by mutations in the CXCR4 variant. We've partnered with X4 Pharmaceuticals to help identify patients who have CXCR4 variants through exome sequencing. Our partners for each program receive de-identified and aggregate data, with a focus on target variant information and associated phenotypes. No personal information (or identifiable information) is shared, nor are any raw genetic data files. Probably Genetic keeps and securely protects all raw genetic data for patients. We are able to fund rare disease testing because our partners will pay for access to data on specific genetic variants. If this feels concerning in any way, it's important to remember that if drug developers or researchers do not understand the genetic variants or better understand the prevalence of specific conditions, they cannot develop and launch effective therapeutics for those gene mutations. One of the most important ways our business model contributes to the rare disease community is that life-saving therapies may be developed and distributed by enabling a better understanding of these critical disease-causing variants, helping to end the diagnostic odyssey for many families. ‍ How to get free rare disease testing Patients can apply for the free testing programs online at chat.probablygenetic.com. Patients, or caregivers, will be asked to share what symptoms they are experiencing as well as diagnoses or testing results, which will help us understand if there is overlap with any of the conditions we are actively working on. If an individual is approved for a no-cost testing program, they will be sent a sample collection kit in the mai,l and they will be asked to return a sample right away by shipping it in the return kit. If an individual is not approved for a no-cost testing program, they will be added to our waitlist to be considered for future opportunities where they may be a match. ‍ What information we collect vs. what we don't We DO ask for the following information from patients: Symptoms Current/previous diagnoses and/or diagnostic testing results Shipping address and contact information (for sending the sample collection kit) Physician information (to comply with telehealth requirements) Photo (optional, but this does help with eligibility, given some conditions have unique facial features) ‍ We DO NOT ask for the following information from patients: Any financial information , including bank or credit card information Any health insurance information , including any insurer or plan information Billing address (we only require the address for shipping the sample collection kit) ‍ 5 simple steps to apply for no-cost genetic testing Complete a quick and free symptom assessment at chat.probablygenetic.com If approved, collect a cheek or saliva sample from home using Probably Genetic's provided test kit Return your sample to the lab using the provided return shipping label Wait 6-8 weeks for your results to be ready Review your results and discuss them with a board-certified genetic counselor in a complimentary virtual appointment. ‍ Frequently asked questions about free genetic testing Can you get genetic testing done for free? Yes, through Probably Genetic's free testing programs, eligible patients can receive comprehensive exome or genome sequencing at no cost. Our programs are funded by research partnerships focused on specific rare diseases and genetic conditions. What conditions can be identified by comprehensive genetic testing? Our genetic testing can identify mutations associated with thousands of genetic conditions, including metabolic disorders, immunodeficiencies, neurological conditions, and other inherited diseases. While we approve patients based on the programs we are running, our testing covers all conditions and abnormalities that can be detected by either WES or WGS, not just those conditions that we are currently researching. Does insurance cover genetic testing? Our free testing programs eliminate the need for insurance coverage. Eligible patients will: Receive testing at no cost Receive genetic counseling following testing at no cost Have their test order signed off by a clinical, telehealth provider Avoid the complexity and potential surprise bills that can come with insurance-based genetic testing Receive the same clinical-grade genetic testing that would be provided through an insurance-based process Insurance coverage is a possible option for patients if they do not move forward with free testing or are not eligible for a no-cost testing program. Insurance coverage for whole exome sequencing (WES) and whole genome sequencing (WGS) varies depending on: Insurance provider and plan Clinical symptom presentation and patient health history Age of the patient (e.g., pediatric vs. adult cases) and age at onset of symptoms Some insurers will cover WES or WGS if:c The patient has a suspected genetic disorder where previous genetic tests (like single gene tests or gene panels) have been inconclusive or negative , yet clinical suspicion remains high The condition presents as a rare disease, undiagnosed syndrome, or a complex multi-system disorder with atypical symptoms that don't fit standard diagnostic criteria.\ There is clear clinical utility and medical necessity , meaning the genetic testing results will directly inform treatment decisions, medical management, family planning, or access to targeted therapies. What is the purpose of genetic testing? Genetic testing for rare diseases helps end the diagnostic odyssey by identifying the underlying genetic cause of unexplained symptoms. Comprehensive genomic testing, like whole-exome sequencing, can provide life-changing answers that lead to: Accurate diagnosis and personalized medical management - Understanding your specific genetic condition allows doctors to develop targeted treatment plans and monitor for known complications Access to targeted treatments, medications, and clinical trials - Many genetic conditions have specific therapies available, and ongoing research may offer new treatment options Informed family planning and genetic counseling - Results help families understand inheritance patterns and recurrence risks for future children Connection with condition-specific support networks - Finding your genetic diagnosis connects you with patient advocacy groups, specialized medical centers, and families facing similar challenges. Start your free rare disease genetic testing assessment - no hidden costs, ever. ‍ Ready to take the next step in your diagnostic journey? Our comprehensive genomic testing program has helped countless families find answers through our no-cost testing initiatives. Apply Now at chat.probablygenetic.com ‍ All tests are performed in CAP/CLIA-certified laboratories, ordered by licensed physicians, and include genetic counseling with board-certified genetic counselors. ‍

body_text: Extensions span both plug-in hybrid and 800V battery-electric vehicle programs 800V traction inverter features latest-generation dual-sided-cooled power module and Silicon Carbide (SiC) based power switches Awards build on trusted inverter partnership Auburn Hills, Michigan, August 3, 2026 – BorgWarner, a global product leader in delivering innovative and sustainable mobility solutions, has secured a major extension of multiple high-volume high-voltage inverter programs with a major European OEM. For 800V battery-electric applications, BorgWarner's traction inverter features a new generation of its proprietary Viper SiC power switches and a dual-sided-cooled power module, combining high efficiency with cost competitiveness. Both inverter families are engineered to strengthen the customer's competitiveness across its plug-in hybrid and battery-electric portfolio, enabling reduced-emission and emission-free driving with high system efficiency.

title: Why Data Accuracy Matters More Than Ever for Asset Management
summary: Data accuracy is crucial for asset management, impacting decisions and outcomes. Discover why reliable information is essential for effective public agency operations.
body_text: Accurate Data Is the Foundation of Better Decisions Public agencies rely on data every day to manage budgets, track assets, and plan purchases. Whether overseeing a fleet, managing IT equipment, or tracking facilities assets, accurate information is essential for making those informed decisions. Yet many organizations still struggle with outdated spreadsheets, inconsistent recordkeeping, and incomplete inventory data. While these issues may seem minor, they can create significant challenges when it's time to audit assets, report to stakeholders, or dispose of surplus property. Simply put, good data leads to better outcomes. The Cost of Inaccurate Information When asset information is incomplete or incorrect, the impact can extend across multiple departments. For example, inaccurate records may lead to: Assets being lost, duplicated, or overlooked Unnecessary purchases caused by misplaced assets Budgeting errors Compliance and audit risks Asset replacement delays For IT departments, the stakes can be even higher. Maintaining accurate records of inventory is critical for cybersecurity, compliance, and lifecycle planning. Without reliable data, agencies may not know what equipment they own, where it resides, or when it should be retired. Government agencies and educational institutions are expected to manage public assets responsibly. Accurate data helps demonstrate accountability by creating a clear record of how assets are purchased, used, maintained, and disposed of. When surplus assets are sold, complete and accurate information also increases transparency for buyers. Detailed asset records, maintenance histories, specifications, and condition descriptions help build confidence and support stronger auction results. Technology Makes Data Accuracy Easier Asset management tools provide organizations with more opportunities than ever to maintain reliable records, teams are increasingly adopting new technologies like: • Asset tagging systems • Integrated inventory management software • Automated reporting tools • Centralized asset databases These technologies help reduce manual entry errors while creating a single source of truth across departments. The result is better visibility into asset inventories, improved planning, and more efficient disposal of surplus property. Accurate Asset Records Improve the Entire Asset Lifecycle For many organizations, IT, fleet, facilities, and procurement teams each play a role in managing asset information. The accuracy of those records becomes especially important when assets are ready for disposal. When inventory records are regularly maintained throughout an asset's lifecycle, agencies can quickly identify surplus items, verify asset details, and create more complete listings for potential buyers. This reduces time spent searching for information and helps ensure that asset records align with the items being sold. Accurate records also help agencies maintain clear documentation from acquisition through disposition, supporting accountability and reducing the risk of discrepancies during audits or inventory reviews. By treating data accuracy as an ongoing asset management practice rather than a last-minute task before sale, organizations can streamline surplus operations and maximize the value of assets they no longer need. Accurate asset data is more than an administrative requirement. It's the foundation for smarter planning, stronger accountability, and more effective asset management. From acquisition through disposal, reliable records help organizations make informed decisions, maximize the value of public assets, and reduce risk across departments. In the next part of this series, we'll explore practical strategies organizations can use to improve asset data quality, establish stronger inventory management processes, and prepare assets for successful surplus disposition.
