title: Why Is Trust the Missing Layer in Your AI Stack?
summary: Why Is Trust the Missing Layer in Your AI Stack?
body_text: An AI trust layer is the unifying trust layer that secures, governs, and keeps AI recoverable across the entire AI estate. It sits across people, data, infrastructure, apps, and AI agents, rather than inside any single AI tool. Key Takeaways A trust layer is a unified control plane, not a feature. It combines identity, data classification, policy enforcement, infrastructure protection, agent management, and audit evidence across every AI system an organization runs, not a setting inside one AI tool. Trade press is already naming the gap. Coverage describes today's enterprise AI stack as built around compute, data, and models, but missing a dedicated layer for trust, as AI moves from suggesting answers to taking actions. The stakes are measurable. AvePoint's State of AI 2026 Report found 88.4% of organizations experienced at least one AI agent-related security breach in the past 12 months, and 21.1% can't say whether unsanctioned agents exist in their environment at all. Trust spans five things, not one. Trust involves people (who's accountable), data (what's classified and accessible), apps (what's connected and approved), infrastructure (where AI systems run and how they are secured) and agents (what's acting autonomously). Coverage must span every cloud. Organizations operate across multiple platforms, AI services, and connected applications. A trust layer limited to a single ecosystem creates governance blind spots, leaving data, apps, and AI activity outside a unified control plane. It's the foundation that the success of your entire AI strategy relies on. An agent governance framework, a lifecycle process, and an agent management platform all depend on the same underlying trust signals: verified identity, classified data, and an audit trail. What Is an AI Trust Layer? An AI trust layer is the unifying trust layer that secures, governs, and keeps AI recoverable across the entire AI estate. It determines what an organization can safely let its data, applications, and AI agents do, established through verified identity, data classification, policy enforcement, and an auditable record of behavior. It is a cross-cutting layer, not a feature inside any one AI product. Gartner has already named this shift AI Trust, Risk, and Security Management (AI TRiSM) , an analyst framework for governing the risk, security, and runtime behavior of AI systems. An AI trust layer is the practical, cross-cloud implementation of that framework: the control plane where TRiSM's requirements actually get enforced across an organization's people, data, apps, infrastructure, and AI agents, rather than a competing definition of trust. Every enterprise AI stack already has a compute layer, a data layer, and a model layer. What most are missing is the layer that answers a much more basic executive question before any of the others matter: “Can we trust what this system just did?” and “Can we prove it to someone outside the room if asked?” Those questions are why the concept of an AI trust layer is gaining language of its own in trade coverage. CIO.com frames it directly: The emerging enterprise AI stack is missing a trust layer, and as AI systems move from suggesting answers to taking actions, that gap becomes the biggest barrier to scaling AI safely. Why Is the Enterprise AI Stack Missing the Trust Layer Today? The enterprise AI stack is missing a trust layer because AI investment has outpaced governance investment. Organizations bought compute, licensed models, and connected data sources years before anyone had to answer for what an autonomous agent did with all three at once. That sequencing shows up directly in the numbers. AvePoint's State of AI 2026 Report found that 88.4% of organizations experienced at least one security breach tied to an AI agent in the past 12 months, and 21.1% cannot say whether unsanctioned agents exist in their environment at all. Neither statistic describes a model or compute problem. Both describe an organization that built the rest of the stack before it built the layer meant to answer for it. The gap is also structural, not just a matter of catching up. Trust has to be re-established continuously as new agents, new data connections, and new integrations get added, which is a fundamentally different requirement than securing a fixed piece of infrastructure once at setup. What Are the Components of an AI Trust Layer? An AI trust layer spans four components: people (who is accountable for a given system or agent), data (what's classified, sensitive, and accessible), apps (what's connected and approved), infrastructure (where AI systems run and how they are secured), and AI agents (what's acting autonomously and under what permissions). Each component answers a different part of the same underlying question: Can this be trusted and can that trust be proven? Component Question It Answers What Proves Trust Here People Who is accountable for this system, data set, or agent? A named owner, verified identity, and a clear line of responsibility Data What is sensitive, and who or what can reach it? Classification, access mapping, and least-privilege enforcement Apps What is connected, and was it approved? An inventory of connected applications and integrations, reviewed against policy AI agents What is acting autonomously, and on whose authority? A live agent inventory, permission mapping, and an auditable action trail Infrastructure Where does this run, and is the environment itself secured? A mapped inventory of hosting environments, configuration baselines, and enforced security controls Most organizations have partial coverage of one or two of these components, usually people and data, since identity and access management and data classification are older disciplines. Apps and agents are newer additions to the same trust question, and the least mature for most organizations today. How Does an AI Trust Layer Differ From AI Agent Governance? An AI trust layer is the broader foundation: verified identity, classified data, approved applications, and a governed agent population, on which everything else is built on. AI agent governance is the specific policy layer that applies those same trust signals to one category, autonomous agents, defining what they can do and who answers for them. Put another way, a trust layer is the platform; agent governance is one tenant on it, alongside the governance of data, application, and identity. An organization can have strong agent governance and still have a weak trust layer overall if its underlying data classification or application inventory is incomplete, because agent governance depends on those foundations rather than replacing them. What Does an AI Trust Layer Look Like Across Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace? An enterprise-grade AI trust layer applies the same identity, data, application, and agent controls to Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace equally, since both environments now generate their own data exposure, connected apps, and autonomous agents that need to be trusted or not on the same terms. Most organizations build a real trust infrastructure in Microsoft 365 first, since it's usually the most mature environment and the one that generative AI (GenAI) and agent tools have reached earliest. That creates a visible trust layer in one cloud and an invisible one everywhere else, which is not a trust layer at the enterprise level, it's a Microsoft 365 control plane with a bigger name attached to it. AvePoint's own positioning describes the AvePoint Confidence Platform as building exactly this kind of trust layer, across people, data, apps, and AI agents – rather than inside a single cloud or a single AI product – with AgentPulse specifically carrying the AI agent component across Microsoft 365 and Google Cloud/Workspace. How Do You Start Building an AI Trust Layer If You Don't Have One Yet? Start by auditing which of the four components – people, data, apps, or agent – already has real controls, and which are informal or undocumented. Then, close the largest gap first rather than trying to build all four simultaneously. For most organizations today, that gap is with AI agents. Audit what you already have. Identity and access management usually covers people. Data classification tools usually cover some of the data. Apps and agents are the newest and usually the thinnest. Close the agent gap first if it's your weakest link. Start with a live agent inventory across every cloud. You can't govern, much less trust, what you can't see. Connect the four components; don't build them in isolation. A trust layer only works as a single control plane; four separate tools that don't share a common identity and audit model recreate the same silos it's meant to remove. Report on trust the way you'd report on any other risk. A named executive should be able to answer, in one meeting, what's trusted, what isn't, and what's being done about the gap. The AvePoint Confidence Platform builds the AI trust layer this piece describes, across people, data, apps, infrastructure, and AI agents, with AgentPulse carrying the agent component across Microsoft 365 and Google Cloud/Workspace. Frequently Asked Questions Why do enterprises need an AI trust layer? Enterprises need an AI trust layer because AI has moved from suggesting answers to taking actions, and AvePoint's 2026 State of AI report found 88.4% of organizations experienced at least one AI agent-related security breach in the past 12 months. Compute, data, and model layers alone don't answer for what an autonomous system did or prove it to an auditor. Who owns the AI trust layer inside an organization? No single function owns it end-to-end. Identity and access management typically owns the people component, data governance owns the data component, and AI governance or security typically owns the apps and agents components, with all of them reporting into a shared view. How is an AI trust layer different from AI security? AI security typically focuses on preventing a specific attack, such as prompt injection or data exfiltration. A trust layer is broader: it's the standing infrastructure of identity, classification, and audit that determines whether a given system, data set, or agent can be trusted at all, which security controls are then layered on top of. What is the biggest AI trust layer gap most organizations have today? For most organizations, the AI agent component is the biggest gap. Identity and data classification are older, more mature disciplines, while agent inventory and governance are newer additions to the same trust question and the least built out. How do you measure whether an AI trust layer is working? A working AI trust layer can answer, at any point, who is accountable for a given system or agent, what data it can access, whether it was approved, and what it has actually done, across every cloud the organization runs, without a manual reconciliation project to produce the answer. Does AvePoint have a product called an AI trust layer? AvePoint has spent 25 years as the trusted layer beneath the world's most demanding data estates — extending that foundation to AI is a natural next chapter. AvePoint frames the AvePoint Confidence Platform as building a trust layer across people, data, apps, and AI agents, with AgentPulse specifically covering the AI agent component. It's a positioning framework describing how the platform's capabilities work together, not a single standalone product. body_text: View All News Femasys Announces FDA Approval of Modular PMA Submission Approach for FemBloc® 08/19/2026 -- Modular PMA pathway advances FemBloc toward potential U.S. approval while Femasys builds commercial infrastructure across its reproductive health portfolio -- ATLANTA, Aug. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Femasys Inc. (NASDAQ: FEMY), a leading biomedical innovator developing transformative fertility and non-surgical permanent birth control solutions designed to improve the standard of care, expand access, and reduce costs for women worldwide, announced today that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved the Company’s modular premarket approval application (PMA) pathway for FemBloc, its investigational non-surgical permanent birth control technology in the United States. FemBloc is approved for marketing in Europe and other select international markets. “FDA approval of the modular PMA pathway provides a clear and efficient framework for advancing FemBloc toward U.S. approval, allowing key components of the submission to be reviewed by FDA in advance of the final clinical data,” said Kathy Lee-Sepsick, Chief Executive Officer and Founder of Femasys. “This approach enables us to make meaningful regulatory progress as the clinical program advances. In parallel, we are building a U.S. commercial team as we broaden commercialization of our fertility portfolio beyond infertility specialists to OB/GYNs, helping bring fertility care earlier in the patient journey. This same team is intended to ultimately support FemBloc, creating an efficient commercial foundation for expanding access to transformative reproductive health technologies through the OB/GYN setting.” FemBloc is a first-of-its-kind solution for permanent birth control designed to be delivered in the OB/GYN office, addressing a significant unmet need in women’s reproductive health. The technology combines a patented delivery system with a separately patented blended polymer that is placed into both fallopian tubes, safely degrades and forms natural scar tissue for permanent occlusion. Unlike surgical sterilization, FemBloc requires no anesthesia, incisions or recovery time, offering women a more convenient and affordable alternative while avoiding risks associated with surgery. Learn more at www.FemBloc.com . About Femasys Inc. Femasys is a leading biomedical innovator developing transformative fertility and non-surgical permanent birth control solutions designed to improve the standard of care, expand access, and reduce costs for women worldwide. The Company is focused on commercializing its fertility portfolio, led by FemaSeed® Intratubal Insemination, together with complementary diagnostic and sperm preparation products, in the U.S. and key international markets. Femasys is also advancing FemBloc®, its non-surgical, in-office permanent birth control solution, toward U.S. FDA approval through the ongoing FINALE pivotal trial (NCT05977751). FemBloc received regulatory approvals in Europe, the UK and New Zealand in 2025, supporting commercialization through strategic partnerships in select international markets. Femasys’ portfolio is supported by broad intellectual property protection and clinical data demonstrating favorable safety, encouraging effectiveness results, and high patient and practitioner satisfaction. title: Why the best marketing campaigns combine video and static ads
summary: Static ads vs. Video Ads? The age old question. Discover why the highest-performing marketing campaigns combine both to drive the highest ROI.
body_text: Table of contents Marketers keep asking the wrong question Why static ads leave an instant impact Why video draw eyes and interest The customer journey isn’t built around one format The biggest challenge for the growing brand: ad production AI is changing the creative equation Better campaigns start with better creative strategies Marketers keep asking the wrong question Are video ads better than static ads? Do you know the answer? It’s a common debate, and a more common question, we get time and again. But, it ultimately starts from the wrong assumption. Customers don’t experience advertising one format at a time, and they certainly don’t make purchase decisions after seeing a single ad. Think about your own shopping habits. You might first discover a brand through a short video while scrolling Instagram during lunch. Later that evening, you notice a display ad while reading the news. A few days later, a product ad reminds you about the products you were comparing, and that’s the moment you finally click through and buy. None of those ads succeeds on its own. It’s a funnel of discovery, consideration, and awareness that gradually moves you from that first brand touchpoint down to conversion and, eventually, loyal customer. That’s why the conversation around video ads vs. static ads misses the bigger picture. The strongest campaigns don’t force marketers to choose one format over another. They combine both because shoppers move fluidly between channels, devices, and moments of intent. Static ads provide often build curiosity. And video can too, but it often provides ways to further dive into your product. Together, they create a more complete advertising experience. The best part? Advances in AI have made it possible for businesses of every size to build both campaign types whether they have the time, or expertise, to do it on their own. Why static ads leave an instant impact Video has been one of the fastest-growing advertising formats for years, but that doesn’t mean static display ads have lost their value. In fact, they continue to be one of the most effective ways to communicate information quickly. You don’t have to wait for the punchline. When someone is actively researching a purchase, they’re often looking for answers rather than entertainment. What’s the product? How much does it cost? Is there a promotion? Why is it worth clicking? Static ads answer those questions immediately. That’s what makes them especially valuable during the consideration stage. A shopper comparing espresso machines doesn’t necessarily need a cinematic product story. They need pricing, product details, and a compelling reason to explore further. The same is true whether they’re shopping for skincare, furniture, electronics, or home décor. Static creative also works exceptionally well for promotional messaging. Flash sales, limited-time offers, product launches, and retargeting campaigns all benefit from clear, concise visuals that deliver information at a glance. They’re a perfect way to capture someones attention when they’re scrolling quickly through their feeds for example. For example, display ads fit naturally into the environments where people already spend time. Whether someone is browsing publisher sites, checking the weather, reading an article, or researching a purchase, static ads allow brands to remain visible without interrupting the experience. Rather than thinking of static ads as the “traditional” option, it’s more accurate to think of them as the foundation of many successful digital campaigns. When static ads make the most sense : Retargeting campaigns Reaching shoppers who visited and left your site without making a purchase (or to upsell them after making one) on the websites they love most. Discovery campaigns Reaching shoppers who exhibit attributes most like your current customers to convince them to visit your website through ads place on their favorite sites. Product launches Quick information about the launch of new products and where the interested online shopper can learn more. Scroll-based platforms Fast ways to get you brand, product, and value across for platforms where people scroll quickly through content. Avoiding Brand Fatigue Easy ways to update how your brand is shown in market to help ensure your audience doesn’t grow tired of your brand and creative. Why video draw eyes and interest If static ads are built for clarity, video is built for attention. Movement naturally draws the eye, particularly in digital environments where consumers scroll through an endless stream of content every day. But video offers something more than motion. It provides context. Instead of simply showing a product, video shows people how it fits into everyday life. A pair of trainers becomes someone finishing their morning run. A sofa becomes the centerpiece of a newly decorated home. A skincare product becomes part of a daily routine. In just a few seconds, video can communicate emotion, personality, and value in ways that a single image often can’t. That’s one reason short-form video has become such an important part of modern advertising strategies. It’s particularly effective for introducing new products, building brand awareness, demonstrating features, and creating memorable first impressions. Even when shoppers aren’t ready to buy immediately, those early interactions increase familiarity and make future ads more recognisable. That doesn’t mean every campaign should become video-first. It simply means marketers should understand where video adds value and use it intentionally. When Discovery ads make the most sense : Product demos If your product often needs to be shown in action, video ads are the place to be. Social proof Video ads are far and away the best way to showcase how your products have benefited actual customers. Emotion-focused advertising Videos are a great way to quickly express any emotions tied to your product, especially when featuring real actors. Building recall Partially because of the length viewing your ad, and partially because of the emotion driven, video is great for recall. Leveraging social On platforms like Meta, video ads usually outperforms static ones and is often the better choice for reaching customers. The customer journey isn’t built around one format The debate around video ads vs. static ads assumes shoppers consume advertising in isolation. To be blunt, this debate is moot. It is extremely rare for someone to be sitting on their couch browsing social media in front of the TV and see a product on their feed that they buy on site. In fact it’s usually quoted to be somewhere between 5 and 20 touchpoints depending on the source in order to drive a sale. Meaning, unless your consumers only consume media on one channel then you need to consider video and static ads to drive the most success. And it’s not just because of where your shoppers are. None of these ad formats replace each other. They build on each other. Where Static ads create initial scroll awareness videos can follow with a deeper product demo. Conversely where video might create an initial emotional connection, static ads can follow with knowledge about a sale to drive the deal home. Using retargeting to fuel these different campaign efforts will drive most of this action. The most successful marketers ask how different formats can work together to keep their brand visible throughout the buying journey. The biggest challenge for the growing brand: ad production If using both formats delivers stronger campaigns, why haven’t more businesses embraced that approach? I think we all know the answer: resources! Most brands simply don’t have the resources—or the time, or the expertise, or the budget— to create both video and static ads. Especially at scale. A single campaign often requires dozens of banner sizes, multiple video assets, social variations, promotional messaging, creative testing, and regular updates as inventory or pricing changes. What begins as one campaign quickly becomes hundreds of creative assets. For lean marketing teams, that’s simply unrealistic. Even at larger companies (take it from one that knows) this is often one of the biggest lifts to creating a new campaign. Businesses will use the formats that they have the time to create. But that’s not best practice and with our constantly changing advertising environment, it’s a bottleneck that doesn’t have to hold teams back anymore. AI is changing the creative equation That production challenge hasn’t completely disappeared. As many of us know, there are plenty of agencies out there that will claim that their expertise will ensure that their efforts will lead to a higher ROI for your brand. But this isn’t 2019 anymore. Instead of manually building every creative variation, marketers can now use AI to generate display and video assets that are ready to review, refine, and launch. Rather than spending weeks resizing banners, coordinating video production, or adapting creative for different placements, teams can focus on the work that drives results: defining strategy, refining messaging, testing offers, and understanding their customers. But be careful, not every advertising platform is cut from the same cloth and many won’t offer this capability. Look for a partner that can help leverage AI to build these assets for you so you can spend your time building strategy instead of building ads. Better campaigns start with better creative strategies Customers don’t follow a predictable path to purchase, and advertising shouldn’t assume they do. Some people will discover your brand through video. Others will engage with a display ad while researching products online. Many will interact with both before they’re ready to buy. Static ads remain one of the fastest ways to communicate products, pricing, and promotions. Video captures attention, builds familiarity, and creates memorable brand moments. Together, they create campaigns that reflect how people actually discover, research, and purchase products today. No one should be searching stativ ads vs. video ads anymore. The strategy should be to approach every campaign with a way to give shoppers enough opportunities to engage at every stage of their journey. If you’re looking for an easy way to build static and video ads at scale, check out Criteo GO. Criteo GO is our new AI-powered, performance advertising platform built from 20 years of really commerce intelligence. Criteo GO not only leverages AI to build static and video ads for you, it also uses industry-leading AI to continously optimize your campaigns to make sure every dollar you spend is driving the most value back to your business as possible. Still skeptical? Take a look at our performance calculator to see how much ROI we could drive for your specific brand website.

title: Biólogo e ESG: como as duas áreas se relacionam
summary: Entenda como o biólogo e ESG se relacionam, quais áreas oferecem oportunidades e como a sustentabilidade amplia sua carreira na área.
body_text: Como a sustentabilidade amplia as possibilidades para o biólogo? A discussão sobre sustentabilidade aproxima o conhecimento científico de questões estratégicas das organizações. Para o estudante ou profissional de Ciências Biológicas, isso significa que a carreira não precisa estar limitada aos caminhos tradicionalmente associados à Biologia. Conhecimentos sobre ecologia, biodiversidade, conservação e impactos ambientais podem ser aplicados em diferentes setores econômicos. Além do conhecimento técnico, profissionais interessados nessa área podem buscar competências complementares em temas como gestão de projetos, análise de dados, legislação ambiental, comunicação e gestão. Essa combinação pode ajudar o biólogo a dialogar com profissionais de diferentes áreas, algo frequente em projetos de sustentabilidade. Quais habilidades são importantes para trabalhar com ESG? A formação científica é uma base importante, mas o mercado de sustentabilidade pode exigir competências que vão além do conhecimento específico das Ciências Biológicas. Uma delas é a capacidade de trabalhar de forma multidisciplinar . Projetos ESG podem envolver profissionais de Biologia, Engenharia, Administração, Direito, Economia, Comunicação e outras áreas. Também são importantes: Conhecimento ambiental: compreender ecossistemas, biodiversidade, impactos ambientais e conservação. Análise de dados: saber interpretar informações e indicadores pode ajudar no acompanhamento de projetos. Comunicação: o profissional precisa conseguir explicar questões científicas para públicos que nem sempre têm formação na área. Gestão de projetos: planejamento, organização de atividades, prazos e acompanhamento de resultados são competências úteis. Visão estratégica: compreender como uma questão ambiental se relaciona com as atividades e objetivos de uma organização pode ampliar a contribuição do profissional. É preciso fazer uma especialização em ESG para ser biólogo nessa área? Não existe uma única formação que determine quem pode ou não trabalhar com ESG. A necessidade de formação complementar depende da função, da organização e das atribuições envolvidas. Para quem já cursa ou concluiu Ciências Biológicas, uma especialização pode ser uma alternativa para aprofundar conhecimentos em sustentabilidade, gestão ambiental, ESG ou áreas relacionadas . Também é possível começar a desenvolver esse repertório por meio de cursos livres, eventos, projetos acadêmicos, iniciação científica, extensão e experiências profissionais. O mais importante é analisar qual tipo de atuação o profissional deseja construir. Quem pretende trabalhar com biodiversidade, por exemplo, pode priorizar conhecimentos diferentes de quem pretende atuar com gestão ambiental ou indicadores corporativos. Saiba mais: + ESG: qual pós-graduação fazer para se especializar na área? Como começar uma carreira de biólogo em ESG? Para o estudante que ainda está na graduação, uma das melhores formas de começar é buscar experiências relacionadas ao tema. Estágios, iniciação científica e projetos de extensão podem ajudar a construir conhecimento prático. Também vale acompanhar empresas, consultorias e organizações ambientais para entender quais profissionais são contratados e quais competências aparecem nas vagas. Outra estratégia é observar os temas que mais despertam interesse. Se você gosta de biodiversidade, pode pesquisar oportunidades relacionadas à conservação. Se prefere trabalhar com empresas, pode buscar experiências em gestão e consultoria ambiental. Já quem gosta de comunicação pode explorar educação ambiental e projetos de conscientização. Construir uma carreira em sustentabilidade não significa necessariamente escolher uma única área desde o início. A graduação pode ser um período importante para experimentar possibilidades e identificar quais atividades fazem mais sentido para seus objetivos. Confira: + Estágio em Ciências Biológicas: áreas e oportunidades Onde um biólogo pode trabalhar com ESG? As oportunidades podem aparecer em diferentes tipos de organizações, como: Empresas privadas; Consultorias ambientais; Indústrias; Empresas de energia e infraestrutura; Organizações do terceiro setor; Instituições de pesquisa; Universidades; Órgãos públicos; Empresas ligadas ao setor ambiental; Projetos de conservação. A localização e a oferta de vagas variam de acordo com a região e com o setor econômico. Por isso, vale pesquisar oportunidades utilizando termos diferentes, como “biólogo sustentabilidade”, “biólogo ESG”, “analista ambiental”, “gestão ambiental” e “consultoria ambiental” . Essa busca pode revelar cargos que não mencionam diretamente a palavra “ESG”, mas que envolvem atividades relacionadas à agenda ambiental. Biólogo e ESG: uma tendência de carreira? A aproximação entre Ciências Biológicas e sustentabilidade mostra como a formação do biólogo pode ser aplicada a desafios ambientais presentes em diferentes setores. A agenda ESG não transforma o biólogo em um profissional de atuação exclusivamente corporativa. Pelo contrário: ela pode abrir caminhos para que o conhecimento científico sobre biodiversidade, ecossistemas e conservação seja aplicado em decisões, projetos e estratégias organizacionais . Para quem está escolhendo uma graduação ou pensando nos próximos passos profissionais, conhecer essas possibilidades pode ajudar a enxergar a Biologia de maneira mais ampla. O caminho até uma carreira na área pode envolver graduação, estágio, experiências práticas e formação complementar. Mais importante do que seguir uma trajetória única é identificar quais problemas ambientais você gostaria de ajudar a resolver e quais competências precisa desenvolver para atuar neles . Se você se interessa por meio ambiente, sustentabilidade e ciência, Ciências Biológicas pode oferecer diferentes caminhos profissionais. Conhecer as áreas de atuação desde a graduação ajuda a tomar decisões mais conscientes sobre estágio, especializações e carreira. title: Why Are Some Singapore Private Homes Selling at a Loss in 2026?
summary: Some Singapore private homes sold at a loss in Q2 2026. Find out why and what owners should calculate before deciding to sell.
body_text: Some private homes in Singapore are selling at a loss because their individual resale prices have not kept pace with what their owners originally paid, even though the overall private residential property price index is still rising. Data consolidated by Cushman & Wakefield for The Business Times found that 4.7% of private home resale transactions in Q2 2026 were loss-making, up from 3.7% in the previous quarter. This was the highest proportion recorded in four years. Yet Singapore’s overall private residential property price index still rose by 0.5% during the same period, according to the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA). So, how can the wider market move upwards while some owners sell for less than they paid? The answer often lies beyond the national index. A home’s entry price, its individual characteristics, the competition around it and the owner’s reason for moving can each shape the final outcome. What is Considered a Loss-making Private Home Resale? A private home resale is generally considered loss-making when its recorded selling price is lower than what the previous owner paid. Suppose someone bought a condo for $1.8 million and later sold it for $1.7 million. Based on those two transaction prices, the property recorded a gross loss of $100,000. However, that calculation does not tell the owner’s entire financial story. It may exclude stamp duty, mortgage interest, legal fees, renovation and maintenance costs, as well as any rental income earned. The reported loss is therefore a comparison of recorded prices, not necessarily the owner’s complete investment return. Are Singapore Private Home Prices Falling? No. Singapore’s overall private residential property price index still increased by 0.5% in Q2 2026, although growth eased from 0.9% in Q1. Yet that increase was not shared equally across the market. According to the URA, landed home prices rose by 2.5%, while non-landed private home prices slipped by 0.1%. URA’s overall price indices for non-landed private homes also moved differently across Singapore’s three market segments: Non-landed market segment Q2 2026 price movement Core Central Region (CCR) +1.8% Rest of Central Region (RCR) -1.2% Outside Central Region (OCR) -0.1% Meanwhile, 3,813 private home resale transactions were completed, up from 3,225 in Q1. Resales represented 62% of all private residential sale transactions. Resale activity therefore remained substantial, even though different parts of the market were moving at different speeds. Why Can a Seller Lose Money in a Rising Market? Market indices provide a broad picture of price movements across the market. Your outcome, however, begins with one particular home bought at one particular price. 1. You may have entered at a higher price Two owners in the same development can achieve different results simply because they bought at different times or prices. Someone who purchased during an especially competitive launch, paid a premium for a preferred unit or entered near a local price peak may have less room to recover the amount later. The relevant starting point is what you actually paid for your unit, not simply the project’s original launch price. 2. Your development may not follow the wider market Even when prices rise across a region, particular developments can underperform. Buyers compare tenure or remaining lease, transport links, amenities, maintenance fees, layouts and competing listings. Even two units within one condo can attract different responses because of their floor , facing and condition. 3. Sometimes, waiting is not practical Life does not always follow the ideal property timeline. An owner may need to sell because of divorce, relocation, retirement, changing family needs or difficulty managing the property’s monthly costs. In those circumstances, accepting a lower price may be more manageable than holding a home that no longer fits. The sale could still help the household reduce its commitments, move nearer to family or find a more suitable home. A loss-making transaction is therefore not automatically a poor decision. The purpose of the move matters too. Should You Wait Until Your Condo Returns to Its Purchase Price? Not necessarily. Waiting may help if holding the property remains affordable and there is a reasonable basis for expecting its position to improve. However, the original purchase price should not become the only number guiding your decision. Before postponing a sale, consider its monthly holding cost, whether the home still meets your needs, how competing supply may affect it and how long you can realistically wait. Buyers assess a property against today’s alternatives, not what its owner previously paid. Holding out for a particular price only makes sense when it remains compatible with the rest of your plans. What Should You Calculate Before Selling Your Condo? Rather than looking at the purchase and selling prices alone, separate these three figures. 1. Your home’s estimated market value Recent transactions in the same development provide a starting point, adjusted for your unit’s floor, orientation, layout and condition. You can use HomerAI to check your home’s estimated value and review recent transactions in your development before deciding whether to sell or wait. 2. Your potential gross gain or loss Compare the expected selling price with the amount you originally paid. This indicates whether the transaction itself is likely to be recorded as profitable or loss-making. 3. What may remain for your next home Your estimated cash proceeds are calculated after accounting for the outstanding housing loan, required CPF refund, legal expenses, agent fees and any applicable Seller’s Stamp Duty. The required CPF refund generally includes the CPF principal used for the property and the accrued interest. This money does not disappear. It returns to your CPF account, although how it is allocated and how much remains available for another property depend on your age and applicable CPF rules. Your gross gain, cash proceeds and next-home budget are therefore related, but they are not the same figure. What Does This Mean for Singapore Condo Owners? The rise in loss-making resales does not mean most private homeowners are losing money. At 4.7%, these transactions still formed a small minority of the deals examined. What the figure does show is that owning property does not guarantee every household the same outcome. The wider market matters, but so do your entry price, unit, development, holding period and reason for selling. Thinking About Selling Your Home? If you are planning to sell your property , start by checking its estimated value and recent transactions with HomerAI. This can give you a better sense of where your home stands before deciding whether now is the right time to sell. Ohmyhome ’s Super Agents can help you determine a suitable asking price, market your property, negotiate with buyers and manage the transaction through to completion. With 73% of homes sold above market valuation, you will have an experienced team helping you position your property for a strong result. WhatsApp Us to Get Started Frequently Asked Questions What happens if my sale proceeds cannot cover the required CPF refund? You only need to refund the amount remaining after repaying your outstanding housing loan if you sold the property at market value. If this amount cannot cover the required CPF refund, you generally do not need to make up the shortfall in cash. Do I still pay Seller’s Stamp Duty if I sell my property at a loss? Yes, Seller’s Stamp Duty may still apply even when you sell at a loss. It depends on when you purchased the property and how long you held it. SSD is calculated using the higher of the selling price or market value, rather than whether the sale was profitable. Is a loss from selling a private home tax-deductible in Singapore? Generally, no. A loss on a home held as a personal investment is normally capital in nature and cannot usually be deducted against taxable income. The treatment may differ if IRAS considers you to be trading in properties, based on factors such as transaction frequency, purpose and holding period.

title: Realtor Virtual Assistant: Close More Deals, Do Less Admin
summary: Discover how a realtor virtual assistant handles admin tasks so you can focus on clients, speed up follow-up, and close more deals.
body_text: 8 min read There’s a version of Tuesday afternoon that every active realtor knows too well. You’ve got two listings live, a buyer wavering on a third offer, four showing requests sitting in your inbox, and somehow you’re the one updating MLS data and chasing a DocuSign envelope that should have cleared three days ago. The calls you should be making — the ones that actually move deals — are sitting on hold while you work through a queue that was never supposed to be yours. Admin doesn’t feel dangerous when business is good, because you’re still closing deals despite it. But the workload compounds faster than your capacity, and at some point, the ceiling becomes concrete: you can only close as many deals as you have hours to give. Meanwhile, the realtors who push past that limit but aren’t working longer days? They’ve offloaded the operational layer, so their time goes where it actually converts. What a Realtor VA Handles: A Full Task Breakdown The scope of what a realtor virtual assistant handles is wider than most agents expect when they first start looking into realtor virtual assistant services. There’s more under the operational umbrella of a real estate business than is obvious until you start mapping it out by category: Listing Admin: A VA can handle the tedious process of entering data into MLS portals, pulling initial comps for your review, and coordinating with photography teams. They also manage the upload process for sites like Zillow Premier Agent and draft the initial listing descriptions, saving you from hours of data entry. Client Communication: Maintaining a high-touch client experience is difficult when you are constantly in showings. Your assistant can take over appointment confirmations, send follow-up emails after every showing, and provide regular status updates to buyers and sellers as escrow progresses. Transaction Coordination: A deal is only as good as its paperwork, and a virtual assistant agency provides the oversight needed to keep files moving. They track critical document deadlines in platforms like Dotloop or DocuSign and loop in title or escrow officers when signatures are missing. Lead Management: Lead decay happens when you’re too busy to monitor your CRM. A VA can manage your daily updates in kvCORE or Follow Up Boss, ensuring every open house inquiry receives an immediate response. Marketing Support: A VA handles the recurring production work, such as scheduling social media posts, distributing monthly market reports, and executing email campaigns to your database. This consistency keeps your brand in front of your sphere of influence while you focus on the “belly-to-belly” work of selling houses. The Deal Cost of Doing Your Own Admin Here’s where the math gets uncomfortable. At $8,000 to $15,000 per closing and two closings a month, your effective hourly commission rate runs somewhere between $115 and $175. That’s what your time is worth when it’s spent in front of a client. Now map that against what admin is actually consuming: 15 hours per week spent on tasks that don’t require your license, your judgment, or your client relationships 60 hours per month (more than a full work week) applied to data entry, document chasing, and follow-up drafts $6,900 to $10,500 in monthly earning capacity, at your effective hourly rate, going to work a VA could handle instead All of these figures represent revenue that you’re actively working for and not collecting. Then there’s the lead follow-up cost, which compounds everything above. In a business where speed shapes conversion, the gap between responding within an hour and responding the next morning isn’t a minor inconvenience. It’s often a lost client. If you’re managing your own admin, you’re also the one returning calls at 11 p.m. or the following morning. Leads cool. Prospects move on. You rarely know exactly what that silence costs you. Training a VA on Real Estate Workflows Training a VA on real estate workflows takes more deliberate setup than a general admin handoff. While the compliance layer is real, the framework for managing it is cleaner than most agents expect. The Compliance Question Real estate operates under strict requirements around MLS access and document handling, and those requirements don’t leave much room for improvisation. Working through a virtual assistant agency means the screening and baseline training protocols are already in place, so your job is to layer in the real estate specifics rather than build the whole system from the ground up. Who Handles What The division of labor should be clear. The VA handles the operational layer while the licensed agent retains anything that requires professional judgment or carries legal weight. That means: A VA… You… Prepares and tracks DocuSign envelopes, flagging any unsigned items Advise a client on whether to accept a contingency Enters and updates listings per your input Make pricing decisions Logs contacts and runs follow-up sequences in kvCORE or Follow Up Boss Handle sensitive client conversations Coordinates with title and escrow on logistics Negotiate timelines or contract terms Building SOPs That Protect You Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are what make this arrangement work smoothly. When you document exactly how a recurring task gets done, down to the specific fields and templates involved, you’re building both a training guide and a compliance record. For the tasks you run most often across Dotloop and kvCORE, one focused documentation session typically covers the bulk of the workflow. The VA follows the protocol; you review anything that touches a legal document or a client decision. How Realtors Who Use VAs Close More Deals The shift doesn’t show up in one dramatic moment. It accumulates across dozens of small outputs that stack into a meaningfully different week: Lead Response Time: Inbound leads get a response within the hour because someone is monitoring them in real time, not waiting for you to clear your queue. Showing Follow-Ups: Every buyer who attended a showing receives a follow-up that afternoon, handled and sent before the end of the day. Transaction Deadlines: Dotloop files stay current, and contingency windows get flagged before they close, so nothing critical slips through a busy week. Marketing Cadence: MLS listings stay current, and market reports reach your sphere on time, rather than arriving late with an apologetic subject line. Pipeline Activity: Contacts in kvCORE or Follow Up Boss get logged and nurtured consistently, keeping leads warm between conversations. When the administrative layer is consistently covered, the agent’s calendar fills with client-facing time rather than operational catch-up. Clients feel attended to throughout the process, which in real estate is the most reliable engine for referrals. Consistent follow-up by a VA is directly related to how frequently closings occur. Getting Started: Your First 30 Days The first 30 days are a calibration period, not a full handoff. A VA who knows exactly what’s expected and how to execute it will deliver more in month two than one who was handed a vague brief on day one. Week 1 Identify your highest-priority recurring tasks and document how each one gets done. Most realtors start with MLS coordination and client communication follow-ups, as both recur every week and have clear enough parameters to document without a heavy lift. Getting the SOPs right at this stage saves significant back-and-forth later. Week 2 Hand the documented tasks off to your VA and walk through each SOP once in a live session to clear up any ambiguity. Your role this week is to answer questions and flag anything that needs adjusting before it becomes a habit. Week 3 Review the VA’s output before it goes out. This is where small gaps tend to surface: a template that needs refining or a step that was unclear in the SOP. Fix them now while the process is still being established, and you’ll rarely need to revisit them. Week 4 Step back from active review on the tasks running cleanly and start expanding the scope. By this point, you’ll have a clear read on where to add more, and you’ll also have real hours back, visible in your call volume and your ability to respond to inbound inquiries the same day rather than the next morning. Reclaim the Hours That Close Deals The hours that move deals aren’t the ones spent updating MLS data or chasing a DocuSign that should have cleared three days ago. They’re the ones spent in front of a buyer who’s ready to write an offer, or on the phone with a seller who needs to hear your voice before they commit. Every hour admin pulls from your calendar is an hour that could have been that conversation instead. A VA doesn’t replace what makes you effective at this job. It returns the hours that admin has been quietly claiming, so you can put them where they actually convert. Magic places virtual assistants for real estate professionals who need reliable support without the overhead of a full-time hire. The matching and baseline training are already handled, so onboarding stays focused on your specific workflows rather than starting from zero. Hire a virtual assistant and reclaim the hours that close deals. Get started with Magic today! David Merriman Co-founder, Magic David is a co-founder of Magic and leads its organic growth. He has worked in the virtual assistant industry for over a decade, including more than ten years living in the Philippines, where much of the world's VA talent is hired and trained. summary: LITTLE ROCK, Ark., Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Dillard’s, Inc. (NYSE: DDS) (the “Company” or “Dillard’s”) announced operating results for the 13 and 26 weeks ended August 1, 2026. body_text: Dillard’s, Inc. Reports Second Quarter and Year-to-Date Results August 13, 2026 PDF Version LITTLE ROCK, Ark., Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Dillard’s, Inc. (NYSE: DDS) (the “Company” or “Dillard’s”) announced operating results for the 13 and 26 weeks ended August 1, 2026. This release contains certain forward-looking statements. Please refer to the Company’s cautionary statements included below under “Forward-Looking Information.” Dillard’s Chief Executive Officer William T. Dillard, II commented on the quarter, “Our 1% sales increase points to a somewhat resilient consumer. Retail gross margin of 40.9%, boosted by tariff rebates, helped grow cash flow and the bottom line. We ended the quarter with over $1.2 billion in cash and short-term investments after paying off $96 million in debt.” Highlights of the Second Quarter (compared to the prior year second quarter): Total retail sales increased 1% Comparable store sales increased 1% Net income of $97.7 million compared to $72.8 million Earnings per share of $6.25 compared to $4.66 Retail gross margin of 40.9% of sales compared to 38.1% of sales Operating expenses were $443.6 million (29.4% of sales) compared to $434.2 million (28.7% of sales) Ending inventory increased 5% Second Quarter Results Dillard’s reported net income for the 13 weeks ended August 1, 2026 of $97.7 million, or $6.25 per share, compared to $72.8 million, or $4.66 per share, for the 13 weeks ended August 2, 2025. Net income for the 13 weeks ended August 1, 2026, includes $37.2 million ($28.4 million after tax, or $1.82 per share) in refunds of International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) tariffs. Included in net income for the 13 weeks ended August 2, 2025 is a pretax gain of $4.8 million ($3.7 million after tax or $0.24 per share) primarily related to the sale of three properties. Sales – Second Quarter Net sales for the 13 weeks ended August 1, 2026 and August 2, 2025 were $1.508 billion and $1.514 billion, respectively. Net sales includes the operations of the Company’s construction business, CDI Contractors, LLC (“CDI”). Total retail sales (which excludes CDI) for the 13 weeks ended August 1, 2026 and August 2, 2025 were $1.455 billion and $1.447 billion, respectively. Total retail sales increased 1% for the 13 weeks ended August 1, 2026 compared to the 13 weeks ended August 2, 2025. Sales in comparable stores for the same period increased 1%. During the second quarter, sales increased significantly in ladies’ accessories and lingerie and moderately in home and furniture. Slight sales increases were noted in shoes, men’s apparel and accessories and cosmetics. Sales decreased moderately in juniors’ and children’s apparel and ladies’ apparel. Gross Margin – Second Quarter Consolidated gross margin for the 13 weeks ended August 1, 2026 was 39.7% of sales compared to 36.6% of sales for the 13 weeks ended August 2, 2025. Retail gross margin for the 13 weeks ended August 1, 2026 was 40.9% of sales compared to 38.1% of sales for the 13 weeks ended August 2, 2025. Retail gross margin was positively impacted (260 basis points of sales) by the aforementioned $37.2 million IEEPA tariff refunds. The Company does not expect any additional significant IEEPA tariff refunds. Compared to the prior year second quarter and adjusted for the aforementioned IEEPA tariff refunds, retail gross margin increased moderately in ladies’ apparel and increased slightly in cosmetics and home and furniture. Retail gross margin was flat in juniors’ and children’s apparel and decreased slightly in men’s apparel and accessories and shoes. Retail gross margin decreased moderately in ladies’ accessories and lingerie. Selling, General & Administrative Expenses – Second Quarter Consolidated selling, general and administrative expenses (“operating expenses”) for the 13 weeks ended August 1, 2026 were $443.6 million (29.4% of sales) and $434.2 million (28.7% of sales) for the 13 weeks ended August 2, 2025. The increase is primarily due to higher payroll and payroll-related expenses. Highlights of the 26 Weeks (compared to the prior year 26 weeks): Total retail sales increased 2% Comparable store sales increased 2% Net income of $348.2 million compared to $236.7 million Earnings per share of $22.30 compared to $15.08 Retail gross margin of 43.4% of sales compared to 41.8% of sales Operating expenses were $887.6 million (28.9% of sales) compared to $855.9 million (28.1% of sales) 26-Week Results Dillard’s reported net income for the 26 weeks ended August 1, 2026 of $348.2 million, or $22.30 per share, compared to $236.7 million, or $15.08 per share, for the 26 weeks ended August 2, 2025. Included in net income for the 26 weeks ended August 1, 2026 are these items: $37.2 million ($28.4 million after tax, or $1.82 per share) in refunds of IEEPA tariffs a pre-tax gain on litigation settlement, net of legal fees, of $104.1 million ($79.6 million after tax or $5.10 per share) related to the Company’s favorable settlement of a long-standing lawsuit involving payment card interchange fees Included in net income for the 26 weeks ended August 2, 2025 is a pretax gain of $4.9 million ($3.8 million after tax or $0.24 per share) primarily related to the sale of three properties. Sales – 26 Weeks Net sales for the 26 weeks ended August 1, 2026 and August 2, 2025 were $3.076 billion and $3.043 billion, respectively. Total retail sales for the 26 weeks ended August 1, 2026 and August 2, 2025 were $2.973 billion and $2.915 billion, respectively. Total retail sales increased 2% for the 26 weeks ended August 1, 2026 compared to the 26 weeks ended August 2, 2025. Sales in comparable stores for the same period increased 2%. Gross Margin – 26 Weeks Consolidated gross margin for the 26 weeks ended August 1, 2026 was 42.1% of sales compared to 40.3% of sales for the 26 weeks ended August 2, 2025. Retail gross margin for the 26 weeks ended August 1, 2026 was 43.4% of sales compared to 41.8% of sales for the 26 weeks ended August 2, 2025. Retail gross margin was positively impacted (120 basis points of sales) by the aforementioned $37.2 million IEEPA tariff refunds. Selling, General & Administrative Expenses – 26 Weeks Operating expenses for the 26 weeks ended August 1, 2026 were $887.6 million (28.9% of sales) and $855.9 million (28.1% of sales) for the 26 weeks ended August 2, 2025. The increase is largely due to higher payroll and payroll-related expenses. Store Information The Company operates 272 Dillard’s stores, including 28 clearance centers, spanning 30 states (totaling 46.1 million square feet) and an Internet store at dillards.com. title: Dojah vs Prembly: Best Fraud Management Solution in Africa
summary: Looking to explore Prembly alternatives? Dojah vs Prembly guides you on the best fraud management solutions in Africa and which platform fits your business.
body_text: Choosing a fraud management solution isn't just about finding a provider that can verify users during onboarding. It's about finding one that can help you prevent fraud, manage compliance, and monitor risk as your business grows. Dojah and Prembly are two of the leading trust and anti-fraud platforms serving African businesses. While both offer identity verification, AML screening, and fraud prevention tools, they take different approaches to helping businesses manage user risk throughout the customer lifecycle. In this comparison, we'll break down each platform's core features, strengths, and limitations to help you decide which solution is the best fit for your business. Here's what we'll cover: An overview of Dojah and Prembly A feature-by-feature comparison The pros and cons of each platform Which platform is best for your business Dojah vs Prembly: Comparison Table Factor Dojah Prembly API & Integration Flexible APIs, SDKs, and no-code widgets for fast deployment API and dashboard-based integration, with more depth on the API side Coverage Government database access across 10+ African countries, document coverage in 150+ Local endpoints across Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, Uganda, and other African countries Identity Verification & AML (KYC/KYB) Document, biometric, and database checks with real-time watchlist screening Document and biometric checks with AML screening plus dedicated vendor/UBO verification Transaction Monitoring & Fraud Detection Real-time monitoring via EasyDetect with rule-based alerts and case management Real-time monitoring via IdentityRadar with device fingerprinting and STR automation Continuous Risk Intelligence Profiled Risk scores users continuously as behavior changes over time Risk assessment stays close to rules and thresholds Regulatory Reporting Audit-ready reports built into the dashboard STR automation and screening analytics via Radar Reports Best For Banks, fintechs, and digital businesses needing verification plus ongoing risk intelligence Businesses needing broad multi-country reach plus background checks and vendor screening Dojah Overview Dojah is an anti-fraud and risk infrastructure platform built for digital businesses across banking, fintech, crypto, and other industries operating in Africa and beyond. It combines identity verification, fraud monitoring, and continuous risk intelligence on a single platform, helping businesses manage user risk from onboarding through the entire customer lifecycle. Designed for startups, enterprises, and SMEs, Dojah enables teams to verify users, detect fraud, and make more informed trust decisions without relying on multiple disconnected tools. Key Features Enhanced Identity Verification: Verify individuals and businesses using government databases, telecom records, biometrics, and watchlist screening across supported African markets Real-Time Data Insights: Track user behavior, drop-off points, and verification performance to gain actionable insights across your onboarding flows Advanced Fraud Detection: Monitor transactions and user behavior in real time across the user lifecycle, with behavioral tracking and dynamic risk scoring to catch suspicious activity early All-in-One Compliance Toolkit: Access KYC, KYB, AML, and fraud checks in a single dashboard, with audit-ready reports and regulatory documentation for easy compliance management No-Code Verification for Everyday SMEs: Dojah’s CheckIn extends identity checks beyond fintech onboarding to property managers, hotels, logistics companies, and events. Pros of Using Dojah 1. High Data Accuracy Dojah verifies identities directly against trusted government databases and data networks across Africa, rather than leaning on a single source. Whether the check runs through documents, OCR, biometrics, or database validation, results stay consistent and aligned with official records. 2. Fraud Monitoring That Doesn't Stop at Onboarding Identity verification is only the first step in preventing fraud. Dojah pairs real-time transaction monitoring by EasyDetect with continuous risk assessment through Profiled Risk , catching suspicious activity as it happens and tracking each user's risk across their full lifecycle. 3. Case Management & Regulatory Reporting Profiled Risk comes with built-in tools for reviewing flagged users, assigning cases, and keeping decision logs in one dashboard. With this, your fraud and compliance teams can document investigations without juggling separate systems. 4. Ease & Speed of Integration Dojah is built for quick implementation; teams can go live in days rather than weeks, integrating verification across web, SMS, WhatsApp, and other channels. Clear documentation and hands-on technical guidance back this up, so issues get resolved quickly 5. Simplified Verification for Businesses With CheckIn , businesses outside the fintech space- property managers, hotels, logistics companies, event organizers- can build shareable, no-code KYC flows in minutes. This makes trusted identity verification accessible across a much wider range of everyday business scenarios. Cons of Using Dojah 1. Setup May Require Initial Configuration While Dojah offers flexibility across identity verification and fraud monitoring solutions, the API setup doesn’t come pre-configured. For non-technical teams seeking a plug-and-play solution, additional technical effort is needed to integrate and customize workflows and thresholds. 2. Government Database Coverage Varies by Country Dojah provides access to government databases in 10+ African countries and supports OCR for documents in over 150 countries. However, access to official databases and verification depth can differ outside these core regions. While document and biometric checks remain available globally, direct government data integration is limited in locations outside Africa Prembly Overview Prembly is an identity verification and compliance platform built for fintechs, digital platforms, and businesses operating across Africa. Originally launched as IdentityPass, the platform has expanded beyond identity verification to include fraud detection, AML compliance, vendor verification, and background screening, helping businesses build trust while meeting regulatory requirements. Today, Prembly enables businesses to verify users and businesses, screen vendors, monitor transactions for suspicious activity, and carry out background checks through a single platform. Key Features IdentityPass : KYC/KYB verification covering government ID checks, document verification across a wide range of document types, biometric authentication, and address verification IdentityRadar : Fraud detection and AML compliance, including transaction monitoring, device fingerprinting, IP/VPN checks, and automated Suspicious Transaction Report workflows Vendor and Business Verification (KYB): Screens vendors and suppliers, validates business registrations, identifies Ultimate Beneficial Owners, and runs recurring merchant risk monitoring Background Checks (BGC) : Criminal history and employment verification, packaged for HR and gig economy use cases FraudLens : An open-source fraud intelligence database aggregating fraud incidents reported across Prembly's partner network Pros of Using Prembly 1. Broad Multi-Country Reach Beyond Nigeria, Prembly runs live endpoints in Kenya, Ghana, Uganda, and other African countries. A business expanding across Africa can onboard users in multiple countries through one integration, instead of using different verification providers for every market. 2. Built-In Background Screening Prembly includes dedicated background check services that support criminal history and employment verification. This makes it suitable for businesses that need to verify not only identities but also an individual's professional or employment history before onboarding. 3. Comprehensive Vendor Verification Beyond standard business verification, Prembly allows businesses to validate company registrations, identify Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs), and monitor merchant risk over time. Businesses get ongoing visibility into who the merchants or vendors they partner with actually are 4. A Shared Fraud Intelligence Network FraudLens pools fraud data reported across Prembly's entire partner network into one open database. Instead of only working with the fraud signals your own platform generates, you get visibility into patterns other institutions are already seeing, which helps catch bad actors early. 5. Extensive Document Coverage Prembly verifies against thousands of document types across hundreds of regions worldwide. This gives businesses onboarding a wider mix of users, cross-border customers, and diaspora users with foreign-issued IDs more flexibility. Cons of Using Prembly 1. Risk Monitoring Is Primarily Rule-Based IdentityRadar provides transaction monitoring, configurable fraud rules, and AML screening to help businesses detect suspicious activity. However, risk assessments are largely driven by predefined rules and events rather than continuously evolving user behavior over time. 2. Not Built for Everyday Businesses Prembly's tools are designed around formal KYC, KYB, and background-check workflows, which fits its core fintech and enterprise base well. This might be limiting for everyday businesses, like hotels, property managers, and event organizers, who need a quick identity check without a technical integration. Where Dojah Stands Out 1. Risk monitoring that doesn't stop at a single check Unlike Prembly, which centers on rules-based screening at the point of transaction, Dojah tracks user behavior risk continuously through Profiled Risk, combining rules with AI-powered data for a fuller picture. That ongoing visibility helps you catch patterns a one-time or rule-triggered check would miss, and respond before risk turns into loss. 2. Unified dashboard for fraud investigations Profiled Risk's built-in case management and audit-ready reports mean your fraud and compliance teams can review, assign, and close cases without juggling separate tools or compiling reports by hand. 3. Trust decisions for everyday business With CheckIn, Dojah brings identity verification to everyday businesses and goes beyond fintech-related use cases. If you're a property manager or a hotel operator, you can confirm a tenant or guest's identity in minutes without hiring developers or building out a compliance team. 4. Technical Support & Uptime You Can Rely On Dojah users report up to 99.9% uptime, backed by hands-on technical support that helps teams troubleshoot integration issues and resolve failed checks quickly. For platforms running verification and fraud checks around the clock, this means fewer disruptions. 5. Full visibility into every identity check Each check comes back with a clear trust score between 0 and 100, not just a pass or fail. You can see exactly why a customer dropped off mid-verification or why a specific check failed with full verification history and logs in your dashboard, making it easier to fix drop-off points. Which Platform Is Best for You? Prembly works well for platforms that need the multi-country coverage plus formal background checks and vendor screening. If your priority is broad documented reach across several African countries and a dedicated background-check layer, Prembly offers a well-rounded compliance toolkit. Dojah is the better fit for businesses that need identity verification to extend beyond onboarding into continuous fraud monitoring and risk management. Alongside KYC, KYB, and AML compliance, you get risk scoring and no-code identity verification, making it suitable for enterprises, fintechs, and even everyday businesses looking to build trust at every stage of the customer journey. To see how Dojah can support your verification and fraud monitoring from day one through ongoing risk management, sign up to get started in minutes.

O Poder da Precisão: Automatizando com RFID Se você pedisse às empresas para dizer qual conhecimento teria o maior impacto na melhoria das operações, elas rapidamente diriam: “Diga-me onde está tudo.” A tecnologia RFID faz exatamente isso, permitindo que os sistemas rastreiem itens continuamente e sem intervenção humana. As empresas líderes estão aproveitando isso hoje. title: Brownsville and Matamoros cross-border payments for import-export companies
summary: A USD/MXN payment guide for companies operating between Brownsville and Matamoros, with practical checks for cutoffs, FX, SPEI, and reconciliation.
body_text: Companies operating between Brownsville and Matamoros do not treat cross-border payments as back-office paperwork. Payments decide whether a carrier moves, a supplier releases work, a customs-adjacent provider has proof, or a finance team can close the day without chasing screenshots. The Brownsville/Matamoros corridor is a Gulf/Rio Grande logistics corridor with manufacturing, port, and supplier activity. That makes banking, FX, and payment timing operational issues, not just treasury issues. Why payments break down in border operations A typical cross-border company may collect in USD, invoice in USD, pay some Mexican suppliers in MXN, reimburse carriers in MXN, and still reconcile everything back to a shipment, customer, or purchase order. The friction usually appears in four places: USD balances are available, but the urgent obligation is in MXN; bank cutoffs happen before the operations day is finished; the person who can approve or execute the payment is not always online; finance has to preserve the rate, date, receipt, invoice, and beneficiary trail. For logistics and import-export companies, the cost of this friction is not only a bank fee. It is the delay, the manual follow-up, and the operational uncertainty around whether money moved in time. Payment checklist for Brownsville/Matamoros operators Use this checklist before the next urgent payment cycle: Question Why it matters Which payments must arrive in MXN? Carrier, supplier, payroll, tax, and operating obligations may require local peso rails What time do approvals and bank cutoffs happen? Border operations often continue after a bank’s normal transfer window Who needs proof of payment? Dispatch, finance, vendors, and customers may all need evidence quickly Who is allowed to convert FX? Manual FX creates access, timing, and reconciliation work Can the payment be tied to an invoice or shipment? Finance needs traceability, not just a bank confirmation What is the backup route? Urgent logistics payments need continuity when the primary bank route is slow or closed Where Coba fits Coba Banking helps companies operating between USD and MXN build a more reliable cross-border payment layer. Where supported, teams can connect or fund from US banking relationships, convert USD/MXN, pay Mexican beneficiaries by SPEI, and keep payment context easier to share with operations and finance. For companies that frequently receive one currency and operate in another, Coba FX Automations can also reduce the manual work of watching rates, logging in to convert, and waiting for the right person to be available. Practical next step Map your top five recurring payment flows through Brownsville/Matamoros: carrier payouts, supplier payments, customer collections, reimbursements, and exception payments. For each one, write down the currency, cutoff risk, person responsible, proof needed, and reconciliation owner. Then decide which flows should stay manual and which should be moved into a repeatable payment or FX automation process. Explore Coba cross-border logistics payments or request pricing .
